articles.title: Premier League 2026-27 form guide: Title race, prediction, players to watch
articles.summary: Will Arsenal repeat, could Man Utd win, what about Liverpool? Breaking down the top clubs’ chances for 2026-27 season.
articles.body:
With the World Cup done and dusted, football’s attention returns to the club game – and nowhere captures the eye more than the richest and most competitive league in the world: The English Premier League.

Champions Arsenal overcame three successive runner-up finishes, and the Gunners are now the team to be shot down.

Manchester City appear the main threat, but the post-Pep Guardiola era got off to the worst start with a 3-0 thumping by Arsenal in the Community Shield.

Manchester United are resurgent, and Liverpool start the season under a new coach after a disappointing title defence last term, while Chelsea have spent heavily under new coach Xabi Alonso.

Here is Al Jazeera’s guide to the five clubs who could shape the title race.

2025-26 Premier League: Champions – 85 points

Opening match: Coventry City (H), August 21

Key signings: Bruno Guimaraes, Christos Tzolis

For years, the question was whether Mikel Arteta’s Arsenal could finally get over the line, and the answer was loud and clear last season. The Gunners conceded only 27 league goals, lost five matches and finished seven points clear of Manchester City to claim their first league trophy since 2003-04.

Rather than stand still and be content with what’s been achieved, Arsenal have strengthened from a position of power, and they appear to be following a familiar blueprint: Keep the core of a winning team intact and add quality reinforcements – the same formula that helped Sir Alex Ferguson’s Manchester United and Guardiola’s Manchester City build eras of sustained dominance.

The arrival of Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle adds another proven midfielder to a group containing Declan Rice, Martin Odegaard and Martin Zubimendi, while Christos Tzolis gives Arteta another attacking option from the left.

Arsenal’s greatest weapon is their balance. They can dominate possession, defend deep, win ugly at times and remain exceptionally dangerous from set pieces and counterattacks.

David Raya, William Saliba and Gabriel provide an impregnable backline rivalled by none; Rice gives them athleticism and authority in midfield; Odegaard offers invention; and Bukayo Saka remains one of the league’s most decisive attacking players. Guimaraes’s arrival could turn an already formidable midfield into an exceptional one.

As with all newly crowned teams, being champions brings a different kind of pressure. Opponents will approach the Gunners differently, and every draw or defeat will inevitably lead to doubts about whether they can retain the title.

Their dependence on Saka for attacking inspiration almost cost them dearly last season. They need goals and creativity consistently from across the front line.

Saka remains the attacking reference point, and Rice has become equally fundamental to Arsenal’s identity, but it’s fair to say all eyes will be on new signings Guimaraes and winger Tzolis, who was the standout player in preseason games.

Now that the psychological barrier has been removed, Arsenal have all the tools not only to retain the title but to do it in style. Can they repeat? It all depends on whether they can handle the pressure of expectations and become an even more ruthless side.

2026-27 opening match: Bournemouth (Home) August 23

Key departures: Pep Guardiola, Rodri, Bernardo Silva

For Manchester City, the new season serves as an era-defining moment – it is the beginning of life after Guardiola.

This transition is made even more complicated by Rodri’s departure to Barcelona, presenting an enormous player gap for incoming manager Enzo Maresca. The Spanish international and Ballon d’Or winner was the heartbeat of Guardiola’s midfield, and replacing his control, intelligence and leadership will be Maresca’s biggest challenge.

Also, City are closing in on gifted Moroccan teenager Ayyoub Bouaddi and chasing Chelsea’s midfielder Enzo Fernandez. The Argentinian international is familiar with Maresca’s style and could add proven quality to a midfield undergoing major reconstruction.

City’s greatest strength remains Erling Haaland.

With 27 goals and a third Golden Boot last season, the Norwegian striker scores goals at a rate no other player in the Premier League can match. With consistent service, City possess a proven match-winner who, in tight games, can make the difference in the title race.

Around Haaland there is considerable attacking variety. Antoine Semenyo and Jeremy Doku offer power and direct running, Omar Marmoush provides pace and movement across the front line while Rayan Cherki can unlock packed defences through invention. City’s league-high 77 goals last season is evidence that scoring is not the club’s fundamental problem.

Furthermore, the offseason signing of England international Elliot Anderson and impending addition of Bouaddi would inject much-needed youth, athleticism and technical quality.

City start the season with the weakest midfield lineup in years due to Rodri and Bernardo Silva’s exit.

The loss of Rodri leaves an unimaginably huge hole at the heart of City’s midfield. Anderson can fill some of what Rodri does, but cannot be seen as a like-for-like replace him.

Haaland starts the new season as a hot favourite to win a fourth Golden Boot and is entering the prime of his career.

If signed, Bouaddi would be an exciting new addition to the club. The Atlas Lions star has been the talking point of European football since his first senior appearance with Lille three years ago, before stealing the show at the 2026 World Cup.

Should his move from Lille be completed, the 18-year-old will arrive with enormous expectations given his technical composure, intelligence and maturity.

New signing Anderson will definitely be a force to be reckoned with, while up front it could be worth watching the chemistry between Marmoush and Semenyo.

City’s biggest signing may be their new manager, Maresca. The players are talented enough to win the league, and the question is how well City will manage the departure of the team’s two leaders, Guardiola and Rodri.

2025-26 Premier League: 10th – 52 points

2026-27 opening match: Fulham (Away), August 24

Chelsea emerge as one of the most intriguing and exciting sides before the new Premier League campaign.

After a series of turbulent seasons muddled with struggle and failure, the London club are set to put that behind them, essentially pressing the reset button.

With heavy investment, the appointment of a new manager and no European football, there is quiet optimism that Chelsea can mount a title challenge. However, the Blues are still undergoing a transitional period and incoming manager Alonso’s biggest obstacle will be to create an identity out of a young and bloated Chelsea squad.

Perhaps the biggest advantage for Chelsea this season will be their lack of European football.

The Blues are expected to go all out in the Premier League and capitalise on their rivals’ congested European schedules and injury concerns by fielding a rested, deep and fresh team for every domestic fixture. Match fatigue will not be a problem for Chelsea this season.

With Alonso’s appointment, Chelsea finally have a plan. The Spaniard’s tactically sophisticated approach and positional discipline will give Chelsea stability and structure, while his ability to adjust systems to opponents and flexibility in both possession and pressing would finally turn the Blues into a coherent team, rather than just a group of individual talent.

The goalkeeper position remains a potential concern, and it’s surprising that for all the expensive recruitment, the club didn’t address it in the offseason. Robert Sanchez is a talented keeper, but his inconsistency has cost the team dearly. He conceded the most errors leading to goals in the entire league last season, according to Opta data tracking.

Another vulnerability might be Chelsea’s depth. While seemingly a major strength, a squad comprising more than 40 first-team players could give any manager major headaches when trying to create a consistent starting XI.

After a disappointing season and failing to make England’s World Cup squad, all eyes will be on Cole Palmer to see if he can regain his exploits of 2024/25 when he had 23 league goal contributions. If the creative midfielder can produce another season of that quality, Chelsea will have a legitimate game changer in their squad.

Morgan Rogers is another player who could be influential. After breaking the all-time Premier League transfer record at 117 million pounds ($158m), the English international is a highly talented and progressive goal threat from central and wide positions who some commentators believe could become a superstar at Chelsea.

Chelsea have strengthened nearly every department on the pitch, and with Alonso taking the helm, the Blues seem to finally have an identity.

Opening match: Newcastle United (Away), August 23

Key signings: Jeremy Jacquet, Victor Munoz, Ronald Araujo

Key departures: Mohamed Salah, Ibrahima Konate

Another title contender, another new manager.

Liverpool begin the season as perhaps the hardest contender to predict. The 2024-25 champions fell dramatically to fifth last season, losing 12 league matches, conceding 53 goals and ultimately leading to a managerial change with Andoni Iraola replacing Arne Slot.

Iraola’s previous job at Bournemouth was defined by aggression, pressing and direct attacking football. On paper, applying those principles to Liverpool’s superior individual talent is a recipe for success – but this is also a squad in transition.

Mohamed Salah’s departure leaves a big void that will not only be measured by goals but also by the loss of the team’s attacking reference point and most reliable match winner. The signing of left winger Victor Munoz from Osasuna is an attempt to reshape Liverpool’s attack after the popular Egyptian’s exit.

The preseason was far from ideal given the departures, defensive injuries and unconvincing performances. The club quickly acted with moves for Barcelona defender Ronald Araujo on loan and Jeremy Jacquet from Stade Rennais in an attempt to strengthen a depleted back line.

Despite all the issues, Liverpool still possess top-class players and an attacking culture capable of overwhelming opponents with pace, technical quality and attacking depth. Iraola’s high-energy football should suit Anfield, where momentum usually turns matches remarkably quickly.

Dominik Szoboszlai, who was one of the few bright spots last season, will be the primary source of energy, creativity and goals from midfield, while the new-look forward line is capable of providing variety and unpredictability.

Salah’s departure will surely affect Liverpool’s productivity in front of goal, but it is defence that remains the biggest concern. The Reds were 12th in goals conceded last season, and they can’t seriously challenge Arsenal and Manchester City with this kind of generosity at the back.

At the front, Iraola’s aggressive style can also expose space behind the midfield when pressing is executed poorly.

Szoboszlai could become the defining player of the Iraola era. The Hungarian’s intensity and technical quality fit the new manager’s football almost perfectly. Munoz is expected to impress with his technical ability and blistering pace.

At the back, new addition Jacquet could surprise many and form a strong duo with Virgil van Dijk.

Liverpool have the manager and the players to beat any team but need to fix their defence if they want to challenge.

Opening match: Hull City (Away), August 22

Key signings: Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos

For the first time in years, Manchester United begin a Premier League season with evidence rather than nostalgia supporting talk of a potential title challenge. After a troubled start to last season, United are in a completely different position.

Their form towards the back end of last season earned Michael Carrick a permanent contract and provided a newfound solidarity that has reignited hope amongst supporters. Third place last season represented significant progress and earned United a return to the Champions League.

More importantly, Carrick restored a degree of identity and stability to a club that had spent too many seasons in the wilderness.

The arrival of Youri Tielemans should improve United’s ability to control possession through midfield, and the Belgian signing reflects Carrick’s intent on constructing a side capable of dictating matches. The question remains whether United are ready to make the enormous jump from good to great.

United possess considerable attacking variety. Bruno Fernandes remains their creative heartbeat; Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo and Amad Diallo can attack opponents in different ways; while the signings of Andrey Santos and Tielemans bolster the midfield.

Managerial stability will also turn out to be beneficial to the Red Devils. With Carrick at the helm, the atmosphere has shifted – the gloom has lifted, and Old Trafford is brimming with hope.

United conceded 50 league goals last season, significantly more than Arsenal’s 27 and City’s 35. This statistic alone illustrates the gap between United and the top two from last season.

The club’s questionable squad depth will be hugely tested by Champions League football this season, and a promising starting lineup is one thing; surviving four competitions is another.

Fernandes remains indispensable. His creativity and leadership continue to drive United, and the acquisition of Tielemans could allow the Portuguese star to roam higher up the pitch and build on last season’s exploits.

Tielemans’s arrival also provides the composure and control the midfield lacked last season. Another new arrival who could excel playing alongside Fernandes in the midfield is Andrey Santos, 22, who can provide line-breaking passes, energy and composure rarely seen in a player so young.

United are still far from the finished product and are not yet ready to compete with the likes of Arsenal and Manchester City. Unless United can add depth with a key defensive signing, they will be up against it to finish in the top three again on the ladder.

articles.title: Dodgers' Tarik Skubal Expects An Emotional Reunion Against Tigers Friday
articles.summary: Tarik Skubal knows he will feel emotions when he makes his return to Detroit on Friday night to pitch against the Tigers only four weeks after he was traded to the Los Angeles Dodgers.
articles.body: ATLANTA (AP) — Tarik Skubal knows he will feel emotions when he makes his return to Detroit on Friday night to pitch against the Tigers only four weeks after he was traded to the Los Angeles Dodgers. Skubal says he hopes to focus on representing the Dodgers instead of dwelling on his memories with the Tigers at Comerica Park. He acknowledged it may not be easy to keep his emotions in check. "We'll see, right?" Skubal told SI.com on Wednesday. "The whole process was emotional. I have a lot of respect for those guys over there. I'm just going to go play baseball." Overall this season, Skubal is 8-7 with a 2.91 ERA. In four starts for the Dodgers since the Aug. 1 trade, Skubal is 1-2 with a 3.38 ERA. He is coming off his first win for the Dodgers. The left-hander had 11 strikeouts in seven innings in a 4-3 win over Pittsburgh in Los Angeles on Saturday night. Skubal, 29, made his major league debut with Detroit in 2020 and had played for no other team before the trade. The deal sent the two-time defending AL Cy Young winner to the two-time defending World Series champions. Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said he believes Skubal has the right temperament to handle the emotions which will come with his Detroit homecoming. "I think, you know, that whole ‘be where your feet are’ adage, I think that’s just who he is," Roberts said Wednesday. "Some people have a hard time letting go, but I think that Tarik is a guy that, wherever he’s at, he’s all in." Roberts said he expects Skubal "is going to try to engage guys and immerse himself with coaches, with his teammates, the best he can. That’s a good trait. Like I said, I’ve only known him a short time, but I’m really, really fortunate we got him on our club. Not even just for the pitching, just beyond." Skubal said he is "sure it will be emotional there just because of the history." The emotions will be fresh because he has had less than one month to adjust to his new Los Angeles home before making his return to Detroit. "But at the end of the day, I’ve got to go play baseball," Skubal said. "I’ve got to compete and do what I do well, what makes me a good pitcher. I’ll probably handle the emotions after." The Tigers are expected to have right-hander Drew Anderson (4-5, 4.09 ERA) face Skubal in the opener of the three-game series. Reporting by The Associated Press.

articles.title: Twins Promote Top-15 MLB Prospect OF Walker Jenkins To Make Debut vs. White Sox
articles.summary: It's Walker Jenkins' time in Minnesota. The Twins are calling up their top prospect to make his big league debut against the White Sox.
articles.body: The 2025 trade deadline marked the start of a new era for the Minnesota Twins as they shifted toward a youth movement. The veterans are gone, the young core is in place and the growing pains are showing up in the American League Central standings. Sitting 6.5 games behind the first-place Chicago White Sox, the Twins signaled they were fully leaning into the future. Following the recent promotion of top infielder Kaelon Culpepper, the Twins officially called up their top organizational prospect, outfielder Walker Jenkins. Selected No. 5 overall in the 2023 MLB Draft out of South Brunswick High School (NC), Jenkins entered the professional ranks as one of the premier prep hit tools in his draft class. He holds the top spot in the Twins' farm system and ranks No. 15 on MLB Pipeline's Top 100. Jenkins will join a long list of top Twins draft picks to make the major league roster. With his debut set for Friday night, he joins outfielder Byron Buxton (selected second overall in 2012) and infielder Royce Lewis (selected first overall in 2017). The 6-foot-3 outfielder has been nothing short of productive in the minor leagues. Across 265 games and 997 at-bats, Jenkins has posted a .303 career batting average to go along with 33 home runs, 145 RBIs, 57 stolen bases, and 187 strikeouts. The Twins have built quite the young core and four of their top-10 prospects could make their debuts within the next two seasons. Alongside Jenkins and Culpepper, the group features 2026 No. 3 overall pick Vahn Lackey and 2025 first-round infielder Marek Houston. With a youth movement underway, all eyes are on how the long-term vision unfolds for a Twins team chasing both the White Sox and Cleveland Guardians in an unpredictable AL Central.

articles.title: Inter Miami Names Cristian 'Kily' González Head Coach To Replace Guillermo Hoyos
articles.summary: Inter Miami CF announced Thursday that Cristian Alberto Kily González has been appointed as the club's new first team head coach, replacing Guillermo Hoyos.
articles.body: Inter Miami CF announced Thursday that Cristian Alberto Kily González has been appointed as the club's new first team head coach, replacing Guillermo Hoyos. "González will officially assume his duties once he receives the corresponding work permits. Guillermo Hoyos will provisionally continue in charge of the team until the arrival of the new head coach and his coaching staff," the club said in a statement. Inter Miami sits in second place in the Eastern Conference standings with 39 points through 21 games. The coaching change comes during a five-match winless streak, with the club recording four losses and one draw between MLS regular season and Leagues Cup play. González previously managed Argentine clubs Rosario Central, Unión de Santa Fe, and Platense. As a player, he began his career with Rosario Central in 1993 before moving to Europe to play for Valencia, Zaragoza, and Inter Milan. He also represented the Argentina national team, playing alongside current Inter Miami captain Lionel Messi during World Cup qualifiers in 2005. Hoyos initially took over as interim manager in April, stepping over from his role as Inter Miami sporting director to replace Javier Mascherano. The front office named Hoyos permanent manager following the World Cup. Hoyos began his managerial stint with a 6-1-1 record, taking 19 of 24 points while the team scored 26 goals in eight matches. Inter Miami hosts CF Montreal Saturday at 7:30 p.m. ET. articles.title: Fabio Quartararo amplía su garaje con un McLaren con solera
articles.standfirst: El campeón del mundo de MotoGP 2021 acaba de recibir un deportivo muy especial
articles.summary: El campeón del mundo de MotoGP 20xx acaba de recibir un deportivo muy especial
articles.body: Aunque las sensaciones que vivan en las motos de MotoGP deben ser mucho más intensas que en cualquier coche de calle, muchos pilotos de la categoría reina de motociclismo son apasionados de los deportivos. Si hubiera que hacer un ranking de los más ‘fanáticos’, en el podio estaría Fabio Quartararo (quizá acompañando a Áleix Espargaró y a Jorge Martín). El francés nos ha vuelto a demostrar el porqué. Antes de volver al ruedo este fin de semana en Aragón el ‘diablo’ ha recibido una entrega muy especial: una de las 50 unidades que existen en el mundo del McLaren 750S Le Mans. Además, la ha recogido en España, en McLaren Barcelona. Se trata de un coupé (esta serie no se ofrece con carrocería Spider) de 750 caballos de potencia procedentes de un propulsor 4.0 V8 biturbo al que complementa un kit aerodinámico de alta carga (HDK) tomado del catálogo de personalizaciones MSO. Su elemento más característico es el gran alerón trasero activo que, en conjunto con el resto de elementos genera un 10% de carga adicional. Algo que Quartararo agradecerá si se lo lleva de track day. La unidad del galo adopta el color Le Mans Grey (también se puede pedir en el papaya tradicional de McLaren)… que es el que hay que elegir para este coche por lo que simboliza. El 750S Le Mans se creó para homenajear nada menos que al McLaren F1 GTR, la máquina que llevó a la marca de Woking a lo más alto del mundo de la competición: la victoria en las 24 Horas de Le Mans de 1995. Aquel mítico deportivo vestía esos colores grises… y también el diseño de sus llantas se ha trasladado al 750 S LM. La toma de aire en el techo es otra reminiscencia del F1 mientras que en el interior había dos opciones cromáticas posibles: Carbon Black con Dove Grey o Carbon Black con McLaren Orange, que ha sido la elegida por el '20' (que, recordemos, el año que viene será piloto oficial de Honda) Algunos detalles adicionales que encandilan de este coche son los logotipos de LM grabados en las puertas de tijera, (tanbien los vemos fuera, en las aletas delanteras) la placa que remarca el carácter exclusivo de cada unidad (la 20 de 50 en el caso de Quartararo... un número que no es casual, claro). En su día McLaren no desveló el precio de esta serie limitada tan especial, aunque si tenemos en cuenta que el modelo convencional tenía una factura superior a los 300.000 euros... podemos apostar a que el de Quartararo se ha ido, al menos, por encima de los 400.000.

articles.title: Drive power past Rome
articles.summary: GREENVILLE, S.C. – Dylan Brown and the Drive’s explosive offense paved the way to a 7-1 win against the Rome Emperors, regaining a series lead 2-1. The Drive...
articles.body:
GREENVILLE, S.C. – Dylan Brown and the Drive's explosive offense paved the way to a 7-1 win against the Rome Emperors, regaining a series lead 2-1. The Drive improves to 28-29, while the Emperors falls to 25-31 in the second-half standings.

A slow-building Drive offense finally saw a homer in game three, courtesy of Isaiah Jackson's 20th long-ball of the year. His two runs driven in gave Greenville an early advantage in the first inning.

Brown set the tone with a 1-2-3 first inning, but Luis Guanipa jumped on a pitch in the second to hit a leadoff homer, cutting the lead to 2-1.

Nazzan Zanetello answered right back with a home run in the bottom of the frame. Greenville kept rolling in the third, adding two more runs on an Antonio Anderson sac-fly and a Ronny Hernandez RBI double to extend the lead. Anderson singled in Jackson in the fifth, making it 6-1.

Meanwhile, Brown dominated the mound, giving up just one run on two hits through six strong innings. He ended his night with a well-deserved standing ovation from the Fluor Field crowd, finishing with five strikeouts for 103 on the season, leading all Drive pitchers.

Jackson doubled in the last run of the game with an RBI double in the seventh, adding to his team-leading 65 RBIs on the season.

Brown retired the final 14 batters he faced before Brandon Neely and Joey Gartrell closed it out. The duo combined for 2.2 scoreless innings to secure the Game 3 victory.

After going just 6-for-20 with runners in scoring position across the first two games, the Drive's breakout produced seven runs on eight hits. Jake Schaffner went 3-for-4, while Jackson went 2-for-2, with both crossing the plate three times. Antonio Anderson also drove in a pair.

Rome was limited to just a few hits on the night, going 0-for-4 with runners in scoring position. Luis Guanipa provided the lone bright spot for the Emperors, going 2-for-3 with his second-inning solo blast.

Brown built on a string of dominant outings by Greenville starters, registering five strikeouts to bring the Drive pitching staff's series total to 37. The outing earned him his fourth win of the season.

Cade Kuehler took the loss after surrendering six runs on six hits across 4.1 innings, dropping his record with his sixth loss of the year.

The Greenville Drive tries to carry this momentum over into game four Friday against the Rome Emperors.

articles.title: Dos Santos and Russell set world records in ‘crazy’ Zurich Diamond League
articles.summary: Dos Santos stormed to victory to set new men’s 400m hurdles time, while Russell broke women’s 100m hurdles record.
articles.body:
Alison Dos Santos and Masai Russell each set a world record while Armand “Mondo” Duplantis won a historic pole vault in a barmy night of track and field in Zurich that would have more than pleased onlooking World Athletics President Sebastian Coe.

“I expect the Olympic Games in two hours,” Coe said of his expectations of the penultimate Diamond League meet of the season on Thursday.

The Swiss city’s Letzigrund Stadium had a raucous sellout 25,000 crowd and the still, balmy weather conditions helped no end for a heady night of athletics.

Brazil’s Dos Santos was first up, clocking a sensational 45.80 seconds to beat the previous mark of 45.94 seconds set by Norway’s Karsten Warholm when winning gold at the Tokyo Olympics.

“I have been showing great form throughout the season – that I am fast, I am strong,” said a confident Dos Santos, with Warholm finishing second and dubbing their discipline a “crazy event”.

“As soon as I knew I was coming here, I was excited. The weather’s good, the track’s amazing,” the Brazilian added.

Then came Russell, the Olympic champion of the US at 12.09 seconds to beat the previous best of 12.12 seconds set by Nigeria’s Tobi Amusan at the Eugene world championships in 2022.

Both Dos Santos and Russell will leave Zurich with a cheque each for $80,000 for having broken their respective records.

The world records were punctuated by a scintillating competition in the pole vault, eventually won by double Olympic and triple world champion Duplantis.

The United States-born Swede came under real pressure from Greek rival Emmanouil Karalis, who vaulted a personal best of 6.20 metres.

Duplantis cleared 6.25 metres for victory, while both vaulters tried a possible world record 6.32 metres, in a truly thrilling showdown that gripped the stadium’s attention.

It was the first time in vaulting history that two athletes had gone beyond the 6.20-metre mark.

“It’s not every day two people go for the world record, so that was nuts,” said Karalis.

The icing on the cake came in the women’s 800 metres, with the star attraction Switzerland’s own Audrey Werro.

Werro also did not disappoint, registering the third-fastest time ever in the two-lap race, 1:53.70, as she edged ever closer to Jarmila Kratochvilova’s Cold War world record of 1:53.28 set in Munich in 1983.

“It was crazy, I am very proud. Thank you everybody!” the 22-year-old beamed.

Femke Broeders-Bol finished second as she continues to improve in her transition from the 400-metre hurdle in which she was twice a world champion.

“Being in a great event with a great time – amazing,” the Dutch athlete said.

Kenya’s world and Olympic champion Emmanuel Wanyonyi held off Algeria’s Djamel Sedjati for a nail-biting victory in the men’s 800 metres.

Wanyonyi has said going for David Rudisha’s world record of 1:40.91 was like running a marathon in less than two hours, and it once again proved elusive as he timed a world lead of 1:41.76 for the win, Sedjati just 0.07 seconds adrift.

“When I see the world records being broken, I know my time will come. There is time for everything,” said Wanyonyi.

US Olympic champion Cole Hocker, the world champ over 5,000 metres, claimed victory in a high-quality men’s 1,500 metres in 3:31.71 ahead of Kenya’s Phanuel Kipkosgei Koech.

Norway’s Jakob Ingebrigtsen came in fifth as he continues his return to the track after an Achilles tendon injury that required surgery.

Olympic silver medallist Anna Cockrell bettered Broeders-Bol’s meet record set last year by 0.05 seconds to win the 400-metre hurdles in 52.13 seconds ahead of US teammate Dalilah Muhammad.

American Parker Wolfe smashed the meet record in the men’s non-Olympic distance of 3,000 metres, clocking a personal best of 7:27.43 to better Moroccan Said Aouita’s previous best set in 1986 by more than 5 seconds.

And there was another world lead in the men’s 200-metres by American Kenny Bednarek, who won in some style in 19.62 seconds.

World champion and two-time Olympic silver medallist Nicola Olyslagers of Australia won the women’s high jump in a season’s best of 2.02 metres.

articles.title: Asian Games: Hosts say all athletes will have accommodation
articles.summary: The hosts of the Asian Games in Japan say all athletes will be provided with accommodation for next month's event, after fears there would be a shortage of rooms.
articles.body:
The hosts of next month's Asian Games in Japan say all athletes will have accommodation for the event, after fears there would be a shortage of rooms.

Initially, 15,000 athletes and officials were expected to attend the Games, which will be held in the Nagoya and Aichi region between 19 September and 4 October.

However, last week the Olympic Council of Asia said the number would be closer to 17,000 after teqball - which combines elements of football and table tennis - and padel were included earlier this year.

In a joint statement, Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games Organising Committee (AINAGOC) and the Olympic Council of Asia (OCA) said they wanted to clear up "incorrect media reports" regarding accommodation issues.

"All the 17,000-plus athletes and officials that are registered for the Asian Games before the closing of Entry by Name in July have been provided with Games-appropriate accommodation," it read.

"Unless there are exceptional circumstances, no further registrations have been or will be permitted."

The mayor of Nagoya and acting chairman of the local organising committee, Ichiro Hirosawa, had earlier said it was "difficult to accommodate this number" because the Games is "operating on a tight budget".

And Hideaki Omura, president of the organising committee and Governor of Aichi Prefecture, had said the hosts had "neither the manpower nor the budget to make the necessary arrangements" for the late influx of athletes.

"The host city agreement specifies a delegation of 15,000 people," explained Omura. "We have not set aside a budget for any more than that.

"There is simply nowhere for them to stay. If they still wish to come, they will have to make their own arrangements."

However, in Friday's statement the organisers said: "The final preparations are all on track and progressing smoothly ahead of what promises to be the most spectacular Asian Games held for generations."

Unlike the Olympic Games, where there is a designated athletes' village, organisers have opted to use temporary accommodation for competitors.

Between 4,000 and 5,000 athletes will stay on board the Italian cruise ship Costa Serena that will be docked in the area, while a further 2,000 will use shipping container-style huts.

The remaining athletes and officials will be accommodated in hotels in Tokyo, where swimming, diving and equestrian events are scheduled to take place.

articles.title: Pipi Estrada desvela el compromiso de Gil Marín con Julián: "En ningún momento le dijo que iba a ir al Barcelona"
articles.standfirst: El colaborador de La Tribu desvela cómo fue la conversación entre el CEO del Atlético y el delantero sobre una posible salida
articles.summary: El colaborador de La Tribu desvela cómo fue la conversación entre el CEO del Atlético y el delantero sobre una posible salida
articles.body: Pipi Estrada, María José Hostalrich, Ricardo Reyes, Ricardo Sierra y Alberto Santacruz han sido los tertulianos de este viernes en La Tribu, patrocinada por Sportium durante esta temporada, para analizar la actualidad deportiva marcada por el caso Julián Álvarez y las duras palabras de Miguel Ángel Gil Marín contra el Barcelona. El futuro de Julián Álvarez volvió a centrar el debate de La Tribu. Pipi Estrada explicó cómo fue, según su información, la conversación que mantuvieron Miguel Ángel Gil Marín y el delantero y quiso aclarar hasta dónde llegó el compromiso del dirigente rojiblanco: "En ningún momento Miguel Ángel le dijo que iba a ir al Barcelona. Jamás, jamás, jamás, jamás". Según Pipi, Gil Marín encontró a un Julián desanimado y dispuesto a salir del Atlético. "Hubo una empatía por parte de Miguel Ángel Gil Marín", explicó antes de revelar qué le trasladó: "Yo te voy a ayudar, tranquilízate, a final de temporada hablamos, y yo te voy a ayudar en un momento determinado a una salida". El colaborador insistió en que aquello no suponía un compromiso para dejarle marchar al Barça: "Están vendiendo que él le prometió una salida al Barcelona y que Miguel Ángel Gil está incumpliendo esa promesa". Además, aseguró que "Julián y su entorno sabían perfectamente que el Atlético de Madrid no iba a negociar con el Barça". Pipi también habló del mercado rojiblanco y de una operación que podría afectar directamente al argentino: "El Atlético de Madrid está negociando con un jugador del Galatasaray, Osimhen. Si llega a un acuerdo con el Gatalasary y con Osimhen, Julián saldrá del Atleti". María José Hostalrich fue crítica con la actuación azulgrana: "Cuando te dicen no, es no. Todo el mundo testa primero al jugador, pero lo que no hace todo el mundo es seguir insistiendo cuando el club propietario te dice 'no es no'". Ricardo Reyes apuntó en la misma dirección: "El modus operandi del Barcelona utilizar al jugador, convencerle y cuando tienes eso lo usas como fuerza mayor para ir al club". Alberto Santacruz también cargó contra esa estrategia: "Quiere fichar de una manera muy concreta, presionando. Todos los clubes acaban cabreados con el Barcelona. Algo estarán haciendo mal". Y describió así su visión de las negociaciones: "Ponen un precio encima de la mesa y presionan de todas las maneras conocidas y legales para que eso se acepte por rendición". Raúl Fuentes trasladó la reacción que ha provocado en el Barça la dureza del CEO rojiblanco: "En el Barça ha extrañado mucho esa vehemencia con la que se expresó ayer Gil Marín". Además, apuntó la versión de la otra parte: "Según Julián y el entorno, el jugador sacó un compromiso de Gil Marín". Ricardo Sierra cerró el debate poniendo el foco en el problema que afrontaría ahora el Atlético si Julián continúa: "¿Cuál es la mejor solución para el Atlético de Madrid en el caso Julián Álvarez? ¿Quedarte con un jugador que veremos cómo lo recuperas?".

articles.title: Sara Alonso y Miguel Benítez suben al podio en el Ultra Trail del Mont Blanc
articles.standfirst: Ambos corredores acaban terceros en la prueba OCC de esta cita de ultra trail, final de las Series Mundiales UTMB
articles.summary: Ambos corredores acaban terceros en la prueba OCC de esta cita de ultra trail, final de las Series Mundiales UTMB
articles.body: Sara Alonso y Miguel Benítez subieron al podio en sus respectivas categorías en la OCC del Ultra Trail del Mont Blanc, con la tercera posición de una carrera de 61 kilómetros y 3.500 metros de desnivel positivo, en las UTMB World Series Finals. En categoría femenina, Sara Alonso por fin se desquitó de las dos ediciones anteriores, en las que se quedó a un paso del podio. Sin Tove Alexandersson en liza, el desenlace de la carrera fue espectacular, con Lauren Gregory y Naomi Lang acabando casi al esprint tras adelantarse por las calles de Chamonix. Tras ellas, Gregory se convirtió en la primera estadounidense en ganar la OCC (6.08:07), entró en meta la española, a 1:04 de la ganadora. "Estoy super contenta, he sufrido una barbaridad, pero me lo he pasado muy bien”, decía en meta. En la carrera masculina, el francés Frédéric Tranchand se situó líder en las subidas más complicadas y se mantuvo en cabeza hasta el final. El campeón mundial de trail corto cruzó la meta en 5.10:08. Por detrás, llegó el keniano Nashon Kiplimo, que había remontado hasta la segunda posición, a 4:29 del galo. Completó el podio Miguel Benítez, que con 5.17:43 se coronó tercero a sus 23 años.

articles.title: Liverpool vs Nottingham Forest: Premier League – preview, teams, prediction
articles.summary: Liverpool struggled to 2-2 draw at Newcastle in first league game of season, while Forest lost to Leeds twice this week.
articles.body:
Who: Liverpool vs Nottingham Forest What: English Premier League Where: Anfield, Liverpool, United Kingdom When: Saturday, August 29, at 12:30pm (11:30 GMT) How to follow: Al Jazeera Sport will bring you all the buildup from 08:30 GMT ahead of our live text commentary stream

Both sides are looking for their first wins of the season, as Liverpool host Forest at Anfield.

Liverpool struggled in their first competitive game under new boss Andoni Iraola , although they battled to come back from behind to salvage a 2-2 draw away at Newcastle.

The Reds are still hoping to bolster their rather threadbare squad and are reportedly closing in on a deal to sign French forward Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain.

Meanwhile, Forest have lost their first two games of the season as they begin a new era under coach Oliver Glasner.

Forest lost both games at home to Leeds – the first a 1-0 defeat in their opening league game last weekend, the second a 2-0 midweek loss in the League Cup.

So both teams will be very eager to find their form at Anfield and get back to winning ways.

Iraola hoping for ‘good news soon’ in transfer market

Liverpool’s new boss said on Thursday it is no secret the club are in the hunt for more wingers after reports that the Reds are edging closer to a deal for Barcola.

Liverpool have also been credited with an interest in Brighton’s Yankuba Minteh and Crystal Palace’s Ismaila Sarr as potential recruits to fill the void left by Mohamed Salah’s departure .

“We cannot talk about players that right now are not ours, but it is evident that we are trying to improve or try to fill that position because we don’t have the numbers,” Iraola told a pre-match news conference ahead of his home debut against Nottingham Forest on Saturday.

“I hope we have good news soon but we are still not there.”

The arrival of French international Barcola could lead to Cody Gakpo’s exit from Anfield.

The Dutchman, who scored in Iraola’s first match in charge in a 2-2 draw at Newcastle last weekend, is reportedly a target for Manchester City and Tottenham.

“When the market is open, you cannot guarantee anything with anyone. You never know who’s going to arrive,” Iraola added when asked about Gakpo’s future.

“I would like to know how the market finishes but I don’t know what will happen with any of our players. I cannot guarantee anything.”

‘I’m no magician’: Glasner already feeling the heat

The Austrian expressed frustration with the recruitment situation at his new club after their second defeat to Leeds, saying that Forest had “ignored reality” after losing at home to Leeds for the second time in a matter of days.

“The fact is that this team had a relegation battle for nine months. Very turbulent season and it ended with a huge effort to stay in the league, and this is our starting point,” he said.

“It’s really very important not to blame anybody because sometimes I tell them facts and they say, ‘Oh, Glasner is complaining’.

“No, no, no. But [our] best midfielder [Elliot Anderson] leaves the club and now we expect we compete for European places because Oliver Glasner is in. Sorry, this is what I can’t deliver within six weeks.

“I’m no magician, no messiah, just hard work. That is what we have to do.”

Glasner should at least be pleased that Forest broke the club’s transfer record on Thursday to sign the talented, but out-of-favour young striker Liam Delap from Chelsea for a reported 45 million pounds ($61m).

The Opta supercomputer has made Liverpool the favourites, with a win probability of 61.1 percent. Forest were given a 18.2 percent chance of winning, while a draw was estimated at a 20.7 percent likelihood.

They have faced each other 124 times; Liverpool winning 61, Forest 33 and 30 draws.

January 14, 2025: Forest 1-1 Liverpool (Premier League)

September 14, 2024: Liverpool 0-1 Forest (Premier League)

March 02, 2024: Forest 0-1 Liverpool (Premier League)

What happened when Liverpool and Forest last played?

Liverpool midfielder Alexis Mac Allister struck the winner deep into stoppage-time as his side snatched a scarcely-deserved 1-0 win at Forest in the Premier League in February.

After a pedestrian 90 minutes in which they barely managed a shot on target, Mac Allister lit the fuse with a stoppage-time effort that was ruled out for handball before rifling home a rebound in the 97th minute to grab the win.

The Reds are missing a number of long-term casualties, including forward Hugo Ekitike, who is recovering from an Achilles injury, as well as right-back Conor Bradley and centre-back Giovanni Leoni, who have knee issues.

Defender Joe Gomez remains sidelined due to a muscle injury.

Alexander Isak is again likely to play at centre forward, with Florian Wirtz playing behind him in the number 10 role. Cody Gakpo is set to play on the left wing, despite reported interest from other clubs.

Victor Munoz impressed when he came off the bench against Newcastle, and may start out on the right wing in place of Rio Ngumoha.

Defender Nicolo Savona has been ruled out after a setback in his return from a knee problem, while injured midfielder Ryan Yates is also set to miss out.

Full-back Neco Williams and playmaker Morgan Gibbs-White are both doubts due to knocks, although Forest are hopeful that both key players will be fit in time.

articles.title: 8 Landing Spots for Winnipeg Jets Goalie Connor Hellebuyck After Trade Request
articles.summary: The trade winds that have blown around Winnipeg Jets goalie Connor Hellebuyck throughout the NHL offseason are a full-on hurricane now.
articles.body:
The trade winds that have blown around Winnipeg Jets goalie Connor Hellebuyck throughout the NHL offseason are a full-on hurricane now.

Via his agent Ray Petkau, Hellebuyck let it be known he requested a trade out of Winnipeg months ago. Although there has been strong speculation of Hellebuyck going to Buffalo around the NHL Draft in June, whatever leverage Jets GM Kevin Cheveldayoff may have had to get a trade done took a substantial hit.

With training camps opening in a matter of weeks, either a trade happens or things could get really awkward. To the Jets' credit, they're taking the high road through all this and keeping matters civil. In what's already, for sure, an anxious moment for the franchise, making things more difficult would've only lowered the offers coming in for Hellebuyck.

There are more than a few teams who could use a player like Hellebuyck and a couple of them who have been thrown into the mix already this offseason before his trade request went public. Although he has a full no-move clause and can essentially pick where he wants to go, we'll examine the lead contenders for one of the best goaltenders of this generation.

Of all the teams who can make the kind of offer needed to land Connor Hellebuyck, the Buffalo Sabres very well may have the most ammunition to make it happen.

Buffalo has three goaltenders with Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen, Alex Lyon and rookie Colten Ellis who played and performed well last season. Luukkonen and Lyon alternated leading the way and both played well while Ellis was able to spell them with occasional starts and stepped in when injuries or illness took them out of action.

Buffalo goalies were good (.900 team save percentage, third best in NHL), but they were also extremely busy (2,383 shots against, 10th most in league) which can put them in a precarious position. If they perform similarly then that's good, but any kind of dip in performance could throw the Sabres into the wild card race or worse. With Luukkonen now having limited no-trade protection, that would make him seemingly tougher to move now.

The Sabres also have young players the Jets would desire. Between Konsta Helenius, Noah Östlund and Zach Benson, Winnipeg would certainly want one of those forwards along with a prospect defender like Radim Mrtka, Adam Kleber or 2026 No. 4 pick Daxon Rudolph in a trade. A veteran who can score like Jack Quinn or Josh Norris would be a possibility, Norris has no-trade protection and Quinn can be a free agent next summer. With Hellebuyck's demand now public, the Jets demands may have to come down quite a bit.

When the Devils sent goalie Jacob Markström to the Florida Panthers in a trade this offseason, the question then fell upon them to answer who their No. 1 would be. While that was a bit insulting to incumbent starter Jake Allen, the question hasn't gone away and now with Connor Hellebuyck out there officially asking for a trade, the possibility of him going to the Devils has to be considered.

A few summers ago, the Devils and Jets were linked in trade rumors for Hellebuyck and ultimately nothing came of it other than Hellebuyck dominating in goal and winning awards while the Devils sorted through injuries and wildly up-and-down performances all around. If New Jersey is going to make a big splash for a member of the 2026 US Olympic team this summer, making a run at Hellebuyck and not Quinn Hughes makes a lot more sense.

New Jersey has NHL roster players they could use in a trade (Dawson Mercer, Arseny Gritsyuk) as well as prospects (Lenni Hämeenaho, Seamus Casey, Anton Silayev) and could move young goalie Nico Daws as well. Allen has a full no-trade clause and at 36 years old, him waiving to go to Winnipeg seems unlikely.

Of all the teams in the NHL that have needed great goaltending to take them over the top, the Oilers are at the top of the list. Subpar goalie play has hurt them countless times throughout Connor McDavid's career, but adding Connor Hellebuyck to the roster would go a long way to addressing that.

The idea of Hellebuyck playing with the Oilers is easy enough to put together, but the logistics behind making such a move happen and getting Hellebuyck's approval make it much more difficult. Edmonton lacks young, talented depth to bring the Jets to the table and there would still be the possibility that a goalie they could send to Winnipeg (Tristan Jarry in this case) would have the Jets on his no-trade list.

Many of the veterans the Oilers could move to the Jets and balance out a trade have no-trade or no-move clauses which only adds roadblocks to an already difficult trade. The odds are low of it being possible, but in our fantasy world where any trade can happen, putting Hellebuyck on a team with McDavid and Leon Draisaitl sounds incredible.

Of the issues the Red Wings need to address, fixing goaltending is suddenly much lower on the list, but once a new GM is hired in Detroit, adding Connor Hellebuyck, a Michigan native, to the roster could go a long way to fixing another big problem with Dylan Larkin.

Although Larkin is eager to find a new team of his own, bringing Hellebuyck in to calm the waters and convince Larkin, his Olympic gold medal-winning teammate, to stay while helping the Red Wings' efforts to end the NHL's longest playoff drought. It could also be the kind of addition that turns Detroit's fortunes around 180-degrees after a quiet offseason of moves.

Although the Wings have John Gibson as their No. 1 goalie, he's set to become a free agent next summer. Hellebuyck is signed for five more seasons with an $8.5 million cap hit. Even if Gibson blocked a trade to Winnipeg, the Wings could put together a trade package to win the Jets over offering prospect goalie Trey Augustine among other young prospects currently in the NHL. There's a lot of wish-casting as well as "ifs and buts" to this, but Hellebuyck returning home to save the Red Wings would be a heck of a story.

It's not a trade speculation piece without throwing the Vegas Golden Knights into the discussion and with Olympic teammates Jack Eichel and Noah Hanifin already there, it stands to reason they could get in the mix for Connor Hellebuyck.

Vegas is never a team to stay quiet in anything and after watching Carter Hart struggle mightily in the playoffs last year while Adin Hill, mysteriously, remained fixed on the bench, it stands to reason there may be an issue in goal. Whether Hill would waive his no-trade clause or the Jets would rather have Hart, the Jets have a goalie they could bring back. But that's a small part of how it could work compared to how Vegas could fit $8.5 million under the cap.

Most of Vegas' players with cap hits large enough to help balance money out have trade protection, be it full no-move clauses, full no-trade clauses or partial no-trade lists. Asking any of them to go from Vegas to Winnipeg would probably result in the answer we're all expecting, a firm, "No."

Vegas heart wants the start player, but the reality of their roster says it would be nigh impossible to land him.

Another team that likes to be in the middle of everything and has been a haven for star players from the US Olympic team is Florida. With Matthew and Brady Tkachuk holding it down, adding Connor Hellebuyck to the mix seems like it would make a lot of sense and help drive a brutal storyline that's developed since Brady landed there via trade from Ottawa.

The Panthers are great about being aggressive and taking advantage of teams in tough situations (Brady Tkachuk, Sam Reinhart, Seth Jones) and here the Jets are in one of their own with Hellebuyck. Making a deal for the goalie wouldn't be as easy to put together as previous ones.

For instance, they've already added Jacob Markström to play goal and while Florida wasn't on his no-trade list from New Jersey, it seems less likely Winnipeg would also be excluded. The Panthers have outright refused to include Anton Lundell in any trade and for good reason, he's an outstanding young, defensive forward. Although the Jets don't have as much leverage as they once did, if there's a way for Florida to win them over, including Lundell would put them to the front of the queue.

But Florida isn't the kind of team to overpay when they've got an advantage, and with the Jets in a bit of a desperate situation to move Hellebuyck, finding a way to make a trade while also making the best and least-roster upsetting offer seems tricky.

We've been watching the rise of the Sharks the past two seasons and with Macklin Celebrini becoming a bonafide superstar in front of our eyes, they're poised to make the playoffs for years to come. A great way to help make that happen could be to be aggressive and acquire Connor Hellebuyck.

The Sharks have a cadre of young prospects with varying levels of pro experience to make any offer attractive to Winnipeg. While they're probably not going to move Celebrini, Will Smith, Michael Misa, Ivar Stenberg or Sam Dickinson, there are plenty of other young prospects to attract the Jets, including young goalie Yaroslav Askarov.

Then again, if the Sharks wanted to assure themselves of landing Hellebuyck, any of those other top prospects would get the job done instantly. That said, Sharks GM Mike Grier has made a habit out of winning trades and not giving up the house the past couple years either.

While teams like the Sharks are surging to roar out of their rebuild, the Blackhawks are struggling to do the same. But if Chicago wanted to hammer it home that they've got a plan and they're going to get back to the postseason sooner than later, adding Connor Hellebuyck would send that message.

With Connor Bedard leading the way, Chicago has a young core they added veterans to this summer with Bowen Byram and bringing back Patrick Kane. With Anton Frondell, Frank Nazar and Artyom Levshunov teaming with Bedard, their future star group seems set. They've also got a load of other young prospects with Oliver Moore, Roman Kantserov, Kevin Korchinski and Sam Rinzel to whet Winnipeg's appetite.

The Jets would ideally want a goalie in return and with Spencer Knight coming off a strong season and without trade protection, he'd be an ideal replacement for Winnipeg to build around.

articles.title: Bela está para volver: "Nos ha pintado la cara"
articles.standfirst: La leyenda argentina compartió entrenamiento en su club con Libaak, Bergamini y Garrido
articles.summary: La leyenda argentina compartió entrenamiento en su club con Libaak, Bergamini y Garrido
articles.body: Fernando Belasteguín colgó la pala en la temporada 2024 dejando atrás una trayectoria inigualable que le sitúa como la mayor figura de la historia de este deporte. Sin embargo, el 16 veces número uno del mundo y galardonado con el MARCA Leyenda no ha dejado de lado su pasión y sigue saltando a la moqueta de vez en cuando para demostrar que el talento no se pierde. En esta ocasión, lo ha hecho en una sesión de entrenamiento junto a Tino Libaak, Javi Garrido y Lucas Bergamini, donde dejó claro que mantiene intacto su instinto competitivo. Curiosamente, este cruce replica el duelo con el que cerró su trayectoria en Premier Padel. Su último partido oficial fue junto al propio Libaak en el P1 de Milán de 2024 ante el 'Califa' y el brasileño, quienes por aquel entonces apuraban sus opciones de clasificación para el Tour Finals de Barcelona. Tino y Fernando cayeron por 6-3 y 6-4 en aquella cita, pero ha sido casi dos años después cuando se ha vuelto a repetir ese mismo enfrentamiento sobre la pista. Con la vista puesta en la preparación del P1 de Madrid y del Major de París, los tres profesionales en activo acudieron a las instalaciones que regenta el de Pehuajó en la Ciudad Condal: el Bela Padel Center, un complejo de alto rendimiento que abandera sus proyectos empresariales tras su retirada. Sobre la pista se disputó un duelo amistoso entre Bela y Libaak frente a Garrido y Bergamini. “Acabo de tener un déjà vu”, comentaba entre risas el propio Belasteguín. Tras el choque, el jugador cordobés reconoció abiertamente el nivel exhibido por el 'Boss': “Si hubiese sido este el resultado en Milán, seguiría jugando, porque hoy nos ha pintado la cara”. Si un golpe definió la carrera de Belasteguín fue su inconfundible bandeja. Sin embargo, el de Pehuajó parece haber incorporado nuevos recursos tras su salida del circuito, sorprendiendo a sus acompañantes con una víbora incisiva. “Ahora ya no me dan las piernas para ponerme detrás con la bandeja y tiro víbora… ¡Y entran!”, explicaba el exjugador. Además, tiró de humor al valorar su evolución técnica: “Mirá si lo hubiera descubierto antes. Hubiera corrido menos, ¡qué pelotudo!”. Por su parte, Tino Libaak quiso dejar constancia del encuentro en sus perfiles oficiales con un mensaje claro: “Disfrutando y aprendiendo con el ‘Boss’”. A la publicación se sumó también Juan Tello, compañero de Bela en su última etapa en activo, con un explícito “cuatro animales”. En el plano estrictamente competitivo, Libaak iniciará una nueva etapa deportiva junto a Gonza Alfonso con el objetivo de escalar posiciones en el ranking y mantener sus opciones de entrar en la lista para el Mundial de Qatar del próximo mes de noviembre. Por su parte, Garrido y Bergamini buscan mayor consistencia en este segundo tramo de curso para consolidarse entre los ocho primeros cabezas de serie y evitar cruces prematuros antes de la ronda de cuartos de final. Entretanto, Belasteguín mantiene una preparación física exigente y continúa recibiendo a profesionales en sus pistas. En los últimos meses, el argentino ha compartido sesiones de trabajo con jóvenes promesas del circuito como Iago Fuertes, Rama Valenzuela o Facundo Dehnike, confirmando que su vinculación con el pádel de élite sigue tan viva como el primer día.

articles.title: Ronnie O'Sullivan loses to Chang Bingyu in Wuhan Open semi-final
articles.summary: Ronnie O'Sullivan says he does not "want to throw in the towel just yet" after losing 6-3 to Chang Bingyu in the semi-finals of the Wuhan Open.
articles.body:
Ronnie O'Sullivan says he does not "want to throw in the towel just yet" after being beaten 6-3 by Chang Bingyu in the semi-finals of the Wuhan Open on Friday.

The seven-time world champion fought back against China Open winner Mark Selby in the quarter-finals on Thursday to seal a 5-3 victory , but he has spoken candidly at this week's ranking event about his struggles.

O'Sullivan has taken steps to prioritise his mental health in recent years, withdrawing from tournaments and discussing his battles with depression and anxiety.

"The disease came back big time today," said the 50-year-old Englishman. "If I'm honest I don't think I will ever get over it."

Artist defends 'unfinished' Ronnie O'Sullivan mural

O'Sullivan, who has not won a ranking event for more than two years, added: "I will see out the next 18 months and see how we go. I don't want to throw the towel in just yet. I've committed to playing until then.

"I want to give myself a chance. I'd hate to finish my career on performances like that."

O'Sullivan lost the opening two frames against Chang but pulled himself back into the match to head into the mid-session break level at 2-2.

When play resumed, China's Chang took control, winning two frames in a row to lead 4-2.

O'Sullivan pulled one back but breaks of 69 and 48 in the following frames booked Chang a place in Saturday's final - and his first win against 'The Rocket'.

"Every time I play against Ronnie, it's a pleasure," said 24-year-old Chang.

"He probably wasn't in the best form today, and I managed to take some of the opportunities that came my way."

Chang will face new world number one Zhao Xintong in the final after he dashed Xiao Guodong's hopes of winning in Wuhan for the third successive year.

Zhao, who won the world title in 2025, took the opening two frames before being pegged back to 2-2.

However, he made two half-centuries as he reeled off the next four frames and constructed a superb break of 124 to round off his 6-2 victory.

articles.title: Could Frederik Andersen’s injury disrupt the Edmonton Oilers’ NHL goaltending plans before the 2026 season
articles.summary: NHL News: Frederik Andersen's offseason injury raises concerns for the Edmonton Oilers' goaltending plans. With training camp approaching, the team may rely more heavily on backup goals, jeopardizing their season-opening strategy.
articles.body: Edmonton Oilers enter training camp with question marks around Frederik Andersen after the veteran netminder was injured during offseason training. The team announced Andersen’s injury but did not disclose its severity and said he is not expected to be ready for the start of camp.After helping the Carolina Hurricanes win the Stanley Cup, Andersen signed a one-year, $2.8 million deal with the Edmonton Oilers. His loss is a big one because Edmonton brought him in to provide experience and stability to a goaltending position that was a struggle last season.How will Frederik Andersen’s injury affect Edmonton Oilers NHL goaltending plans?The Edmonton Oilers could be forced to lean more on their backup options in goal while they await an update on Frederik Andersen’s availability due to injury.The Edmonton Oilers bolstered a key area of weakness by signing Frederik Andersen. The Danish goalie, 36, played in the NHL for 13 seasons with the Anaheim Ducks, Toronto Maple Leafs and Carolina Hurricanes.In the 2025-26 regular season, Andersen had a.874 save percentage and a 3.05 goals-against average in 35 starts for the Carolina Hurricanes. His numbers weren't spectacular, but he was noticeably better in the playoffs.During the Hurricanes’ run to the Stanley Cup, Andersen was 13-2 with a 1.89 goals-against average.910 save percentage and three shutouts in 16 games. That playoff experience was a big reason Edmonton liked him.What is known about Frederik Andersen’s injury?The Edmonton Oilers did not divulge the type of injury Frederik Andersen sustained in the offseason or how serious it is. The team has also not set a timetable for his return.That uncertainty makes his status particularly important with training camp approaching. Edmonton said another update will come when appropriate, leaving the team and its fans with no clear indication whether Andersen might be back early in the season.With Andersen out of training camp, the expectation is that goalies Tristan Jarry and Devon Levi will get a few extra looks from the Edmonton Oilers.Andersen is out of action, so this could be an opportunity for Jarry to take on a bigger role. Meanwhile, Levi would get valuable NHL exposure if Edmonton handles its crease well through camp and the preseason.The vacancy also provides the organization an opportunity to test its depth before making any further decisions.Why does Andersen’s absence matter for the NHL season?Timing is particularly important as Edmonton was already looking to get better in net. The Oilers ended last season with a .883 team save percentage, which was among the worst in the NHL.Edmonton’s training camp opens Sept. 16, and the Oilers face the Winnipeg Jets in their first pre-season game on Sept. 19. The Oilers open the regular season on September 29 against the Vancouver Canucks.If Andersen is healthy enough to stay on the sideline into the regular season, Edmonton could be under immediate pressure to find a reliable answer in net. His eventual return could be one of the key storylines early in the season for the Oilers.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Will Auston Matthews make the NHL top 10 despite recent concerns surrounding his Toronto Maple Leafs performance
articles.summary: NHL News: Auston Matthews is under scrutiny for his performance in the 2025-26 NHL season, raising questions about his position in the top 10 as we approach TSN's new player rankings. After an injury-riddled season, analysts debate if he still deserves the elite status.
articles.body: Auston Matthews’ tough 2025-26 season with the Toronto Maple Leafs has made talk of whether he will remain inside the top 10 in the NHL a talking point. TSN’s Bryan Hayes and Frank Corrado were talking recently about where the star center might land in the network’s upcoming player rankings, and Corrado was especially skeptical.The debate follows NHL Network ranking Matthews No. 8 on its list of the top 20 centers. That ranking also had Montreal Canadiens captain Nick Suzuki ninth with 101 points and a Selke Trophy win, adding to the debate about where Matthews stands right now.Why could Auston Matthews miss TSN’s NHL top 10?The biggest issue is Matthews’ recent production and availability. Frank Corrado believes Matthews could drop out of TSN’s top 10, while Bryan Hayes also questioned whether the Toronto Maple Leafs captain is currently worthy of a spot in the top 15 players in the league.Matthews finished the 2025-26 season with 27 goals and 53 points in 60 games, the lowest totals of his 10-season NHL career. He was injured for 22 games, but still became the all-time goal-scoring leader of the Toronto Maple Leafs.That drop is especially significant because Matthews had become one of the NHL’s top goal scorers. Before last season, he had scored at least 30 goals in each of the previous nine seasons.Frank Corrado questions Matthews’ current NHL statusCorrado already has Matthews outside the top 10, which means the center could fall somewhere in the No. 17-to-25 range in TSN’s upcoming ranking. His view is less about Matthews’ career to date than his recent form.Matthews could fall out of the top 10 due to the way he has played over the last two seasons, Hayes argued. Where Matthews ends up on TSN's new Top 50 list is a mystery, as it has yet to be released.Matthews’ ranking by the NHL Network has also drawn comparisons to Nick Suzuki. Suzuki finished with 101 points in 82 games, won the Selke Trophy and helped the Canadiens reach the Eastern Conference Final.Matthews was eighth, and Suzuki was ninth among centers. Matthews’ standing as one of the NHL’s best has grown increasingly uncertain heading into the new season, following the gap in 2025-26 results.So the upcoming TSN ranking could be an important indicator of how NHL analysts view Matthews’ standing after a campaign cut short by injury.Auston Matthews’ status among the NHL’s best players is being challenged ahead of TSN’s upcoming Top 50 ranking. The Toronto Maple Leafs captain recorded 53 points in 60 games before his 2025-26 season ended due to injury. Analysts Bryan Hayes and Frank Corrado can't agree if Matthews still deserves a top-10 spot going into the 2026-27 season.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: What did Nick Suzuki’s salary comments reveal about Montreal Canadiens’ future NHL contract strategy
articles.summary: NHL News: Nick Suzuki discusses the shifts in NHL salary dynamics and how his team-first mentality could impact future contract negotiations for the Montreal Canadiens as they navigate the financial landscape.
articles.body: Nick Suzuki’s remarks highlight the growing chasm between his present Montreal Canadiens deal and NHL superstar salaries. The captain says he knows how much the league’s financial landscape has shifted since he signed his long-term deal. His comments also emphasized how important a victory in Montreal would be, especially with the Canadiens about to begin contract talks with some of their top players.Nick Suzuki has become a key player for the Montreal Canadiens, and his present contract is more team-friendly than the biggest deals in the league. Therefore, his comments could affect the way fans view the organization regarding future contracts and salary expectations.Why Nick Suzuki addressed the Montreal Canadiens’ changing NHL salary landscapeThe salary landscape is changing in the NHL, said Nick Suzuki, who said long-term contracts can quickly become outdated as salaries rise around the league.Suzuki is under a long-term contract he signed with the Montreal Canadiens with an annual salary cap hit of $7.875 million. The financial landscape for NHL stars has changed a lot in those five years of that deal.The comparison is even more telling when you look at contracts for the league’s highest-paid players. Look at Leon Draisaitl making $14 million per year, and one can see how far the high end of the NHL market has come.This is particularly interesting considering Suzuki is Montreal's captain. Instead of publicly complaining about being paid under what the current market dictates, he understood that signing a long-term deal has the potential to be underpaid at some point in the future.The focus in the Montreal Canadiens’ locker room is on winning, not on maximizing individual salaries, said Suzuki.His comments indicated some players have chosen to forego more money to join or remain in Montreal due to the team's competitive ambitions. That mindset could be important as the Canadiens navigate future contract talks.Suzuki also said that NHL players are paid enough to know they’re set for the long haul financially, which makes his comments less about personal pay and more about the priorities of team-building.How could Nick Suzuki’s comments affect Montreal?Suzuki’s standing could provide Montreal Canadiens general manager Kent Hughes with some extra wiggle room when considering future contracts. A captain who puts winning above maximizing salary can help build a team-first culture as the organization tries to build around its core.In the end, NHL contracts are a product of the individual circumstances, market value and leverage at the negotiating table. Suzuki’s comments are not to be interpreted as every Montreal player accepting less than market value.The upside in the short term is undeniable: Suzuki is locked up on a contract that looks more and more advantageous relative to the NHL’s top salaries. That gives Montreal the ability to use some of that room to add cap space elsewhere, while still building around its captain.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: El K4 500 y Laia Pelachs inauguran el medallero español en el Mundial con dos platas
articles.standfirst: El cuarteto formado por Sara Ouzande, Lucía Val, Daniela García y Bárbara Pardo refrenda otro éxito, al que se ha unido Pelachs en la primera jornada de finales del campeonato
articles.summary: El cuarteto formado por Sara Ouzande, Lucía Val, Daniela García y Bárbara Pardo refrenda otro éxito, al que se ha unido Pelachs en la primera jornada de finales del campeonato
articles.body: El K4 500 femenino español no se baja del podio. En las dos últimas temporadas, el cuarteto, formado ahora por Sara Ouzande, Lucía Val, Daniela García y Bárbara Pardo, ha encadenado éxitos tanto en Copas del Mundo como en el Europeo y el pasado Mundial. En Poznan, donde este viernes se disputó la primera jornada de finales del campeonato universal, el K4 volvió a demostrar su enorme regularidad para proclamarse subcampeón del mundo e inaugurar el medallero del equipo español, que completó minutos después Laia Pelachs con otra plata en K1 1.000 metros. El K4, que defendía del oro logrado el pasado año en Milán, tenía como objetivo volver a subir al podio, conscientes de que China se erigía en su gran rival, ya que había superado al barco español en las Copas del Mundo de Szeged, Brandemburgo y Montreal. Desde el inicio, el equipo chino, con Yu, Yin, Wang y Shen, se situó primero para liderar una final en la que España siempre estuvo al acecho, en segunda posición, pero sin poder lograr rebasarlas antes de alcanzar la meta. El oro fue para China (1:38.67), por delante del cuarteto español (1:39.91), que sólo aventajó en dos centésimas a Alemania, que completó el podio. Minutos después, Laia Pelachs sumó la segunda medalla para el equipo español, otra plata, esta vez en K1 1.000 metros, con la que la palista se estrena en esta cita mundial. Con una sólida carrera, la española siempre fue en segunda posición (4:14.76), tras la húngara Zsoka Csikos (4:11.95), que se colgó el oro. El bronce fue para la danesa Pernille Brandstrup Knudsen (4:17.30). El renovado K4 500 masculino, que ya sin Saúl Craviotto forma ahora con Adrián del Río, Marcus Cooper, Carlos Arevalo y Rodrigo Germade, no pudo subir al podio y acabó octavo la final, con un tiempo de 1:26.91, lejos de la potente embarcación alemana de Rendschmidt, Lemke, Schopf y Liebscher-Lucz (1:23.95). Completaron el podio Australia y Portugal. En la final de C2 500, Angels Moreno y Viktoria Yarchevska lucharon hasta los últimos metros, pero acabaron quintas (2:03.55), mientras que Pablo Crespo fue sexto en C1 1000 y Pablo Graña quinto en C1 200 a tres décimas del podio que cerró el ruso Zholabau. En paracanoe, David González acabó en la sexta plaza en la final de VL1 200 metros.
