articles.title: Fantasy Football: From Jaxson Dart to Parker Washington, we present the 2026 All-Breakout Team
articles.summary: Matt Okada presents his All-Breakout team for 2026 fantasy football.
articles.body:
There are several different avenues to winning a fantasy championship, but one of the most tried and true is identifying and drafting breakout players. Very few teams that drafted Drake Maye and Jaxon Smith-Njigba at their preseason prices last year fell short of the goal. Finding a superstar in the middle rounds, or an every-week starter at the end of drafts, is an advantage worth pursuing year in and year out.

So who are the "Diamonds in the Rough" for the upcoming season? May I present the 2026 All-Breakout Team.

Note: I'm not considering rookies for this article, only players with previously established expectations.

Highest Finish : QB13 in 2025 (rookie year)

Frankly, picking Jaxson Dart here is almost cheating, as he was actually superb for fantasy as the Giants' starter last season. In the 12 contests Dart started, he averaged 20.13 fantasy points per game, which would have been good for QB5 behind only Josh Allen (21.45), Drake Maye (20.67), Matthew Stafford (20.61) and Patrick Mahomes (20.37) — and more or less in the same tier as the latter four.

His secret weapon: rushing. Dart rushed for 40.6 yards per game and nine touchdowns in his 12 starts. Projected for a full season, that would be 690 yards and 12-13 touchdowns ... marks that have only ever been hit in unison by Cam Newton and Jalen Hurts.

Despite all this, Dart is just the QB11 in Yahoo ADP, as drafters seem to remember the injuries that shortened his season more than the healthy production. Which is why it's not cheating to pick him as our breakout QB. Perhaps best of all: Dart logged much of his rookie production without Malik Nabers or Cam Skattebo, both of whom are on track to start the season healthy. Pending health, Dart should be better as a passer in Year 2 and maintain his rare rushing upside — a combination poised to catapult him into the elite tier of fantasy quarterbacks.

No, that "RB115 in 2024" is not a typo. In the two years since he was drafted 46th overall, Jonathon Brooks has a grand total of 22 rushing yards, 23 receiving yards and no touchdowns, in just three games played back in 2024. He's spent most of the past couple dozen months recovering from knee injuries, but is finally healthy entering 2026 ( knock on wood ). While analysts and ADP have had Chuba Hubbard ahead of Brooks for most of this offseason, I've spent most of that time disagreeing (and the duo has recently flipped).

Why? Well, Brooks was a high second-round pick for a reason ... or several, really. He's a smooth, explosive and efficient runner with pass-catching chops and good size. For context, here are the eight running backs selected with a pick in the first half of Round 2 prior to Brooks: Kenneth Walker III, Breece Hall, Javonte Williams, Jonathan Taylor, D'Andre Swift, Nick Chubb, Dalvin Cook, Derrick Henry. Every single one of those running backs has seen a legitimate breakout at some point in their career, and most of them have been fantasy RB1s at least once. Hubbard has been sidelined with a hamstring injury, and the next back on the depth chart is Trevor Etienne. In other words, Brooks has a chance to win this job and run with it right out the gate.

I'll admit it up front: I liked Jordan Mason as a breakout candidate last season, and he barely finished as an RB3. I'm not giving up just yet. Over the last two years, Mason has forced a missed tackle on 33.9% of his carries and logged a 14.4% explosive run rate. Among the 44 running backs with 200+ carries in that span, he ranks No. 1 in both those metrics . He has prototypical size, at 5-foot-11, 230 pounds, and has already starred in a leading role. In the 10 games he's seen 10+ carries since 2024 — mostly while starting in place of an injured Christian McCaffrey or Aaron Jones Sr. — Mason has averaged 12.9 fantasy points per game with six rushing touchdowns. That mark of 12.9 PPG would have been good for RB17 last year ... just ahead of Ashton Jeanty.

The primary roadblock to Mason's breakout is the presence of Jones. But at 31 years old, Jones has pretty clearly hit the veteran decline and might be better suited as a pass-catcher and change-of-pace back in Minnesota. If Mason can prove himself early, and Kevin O'Connell hands him the reins to the backfield, he'll have major breakout potential and high-end RB2 upside.

Parker Washington is, without a doubt, my No. 1 "ride-or-die" or "flag-plant" player for 2026. His breakout technically started over the latter half of last year, but he's still just the WR30 in Yahoo ADP, even after a precipitous preseason climb, so the fantasy community has yet to buy all the way in.

Here's what you need to know. Over the final nine games of the regular season and the Wild Card Round, Washington averaged 13.4 fantasy points per game, with 74.7 yards per game and five touchdowns. When Washington, Brian Thomas Jr. and Jakobi Meyers were all on the field together after the Week 8 bye, Washington led the team with a 31% target share and averaged an elite 3.17 yards per route run. Josh Norris, Hayden Winks and Matt Harmon highlighted Washington back in July, and he's only gained more traction as the top receiver in Duval since. Heck, the Jaguars even put Washington front and center in the social campaign for their new Rivalries uniforms this month.

I've been battling with myself over Washington's current spot in my rankings (WR22), and might find a way to get him a spot or two higher before opening weekend. Either way, draft him as your WR2 or WR3 in the middle rounds and thank me later.

I actually have Luther Burden III just a little bit lower than ADP, but even as my WR27, he's a major breakout candidate following a rookie season with just 47 catches, 652 yards and two touchdowns. Burden was heavily out-snapped by DJ Moore and even Olamide Zaccheaus last year, but both wide receivers are gone entering 2026. And when Burden was on the field, he was exceptional, averaging 2.7 yards per route run. Among all wide receivers with 200+ routes in 2025, that ranked third, behind ... Puka Nacua and Jaxon Smith-Njigba.

Heading into the second year of Ben Johnson's offense in Chicago and the third of Caleb Williams' budding career, Burden is poised to take a major leap in playtime, which should come with a major leap in usage. He should also benefit from positive regression in the touchdown department, as scoring just twice on 47 catches is unreasonably inefficient. He has to battle Rome Odunze and Colston Loveland for targets, which could lead to some week-to-week inconsistency and is the only reason I haven't personally ranked him higher. But I'd wager Burden's more likely to double his fantasy numbers from his rookie year than he is to maintain the status quo. If you have a chance to get him in the sixth or seventh round, do it.

When John Harbaugh's Giants signed Isaiah Likely back in March, my interest was immediately piqued. A new head coach instantly targeting a player from his previous team, who never really got an extended chance to be the starter, as a key cog in a fresh offense? Sign me up. Mark Andrews kept Likely from a proper fantasy breakout for years in Baltimore, but he now has a chance to shine as the TE1 in New York.

Over his four-year career, Likely has averaged 11.6 yards per catch and scored 15 touchdowns. Only one tight end over that span has more touchdowns and a higher yards-per-reception average ... and his name is George Kittle. Take that efficiency and red-zone prowess, ratchet the targets up from the 50-60 range to the 80-90 range, and you have the perfect recipe for a tight end breakout. Likely and Dart form one of my favorite sneakier stacks in fantasy this year, and the 26-year-old tight end is extremely cheap, going as the TE13 in the 10th round. If you miss out on an elite option like Brock Bowers, or my favorite consolation in Tucker Kraft, consider pivoting to Likely for a late value.

I know what you're thinking. It's the Cleveland Browns. Shouldn't we be avoiding them like the plague in fantasy? Well, I'm not so sure, particularly when it comes to second-year running back Quinshon Judkins. No, Deshaun Watson does not inspire confidence as the starting quarterback. But the Browns heavily reworked their offensive line this offseason and added a pair of dynamic young receivers in KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston. Those are undeniable improvements around Judkins, who was the RB18 from his Week 2 debut through Week 15 (before his fractured fibula in Week 16).

The same historical draft capital context I supplied for Brooks above applies to Judkins — who went 36th overall — and he has an even better chance at true bell-cow volume in Cleveland. As for that O-line I mentioned, get this: 93.3% of Judkins' rookie rushing yards came after contact , the highest rate among the 49 RBs with 100+ carries last season. On a better team, I might project Judkins for an RB1 season. But even on the Browns, he's a prime breakout candidate with high-end RB2 potential.

articles.title: WWE Wrestlepalooza Date, Location Announced amid Rumors of John Cena Classic Tournament 2026
articles.summary: WWE announced Thursday that the Wrestlepalooza premium live event will be held at RAC Arena in Perth, Western Australia, on Dec. 12, 2026.
articles.body:
WWE announced Thursday that the Wrestlepalooza premium live event will be held at RAC Arena in Perth, Western Australia, on Dec. 12, 2026.

The venue will also play host to SmackDown on Dec. 11 and Raw on Dec. 14 as part of an expanded partnership between WWE and Western Australia through 2028.

It was previously reported by False Finish that WWE was "looking at" holding the John Cena Classic tournament on Dec. 12 at a yet-to-be-determined location.

Dave Meltzer of the Wrestling Observer Newsletter (h/t Wrestle Features ) followed up by reporting Friday that the John Cena Classic will indeed take place on Dec. 12, but he too did not have details on the location.

Since it seems unlikely that WWE would have two major shows on the same day, signs point toward the John Cena Classic being part of the Wrestlepalooza PLE in Perth.

articles.title: Enes Kanter Freedom pushes back after Cameron Brink dismisses transgender athlete debate as 'non-issue'
articles.summary: Freedom spoke out after being barred from Chicago Sky games following his baseline confrontation with WNBA guard Natasha Cloud in the third quarter.
articles.body: Former NBA player Enes Kanter Freedom was ejected from Sunday’s Chicago Sky game after a confrontation with guard Natasha Cloud late in the third quarter. Freedom had been seated along the baseline wearing a black shirt that read, "WOMAN noun. adult human female." The Sky later announced that the 6-foot-10, 250-pound former NBA center would be barred from future games at Wintrust Arena. Team owner Michael Alter said the ban would remain in place "unless sometime in the future he’s able to prove to us to our satisfaction that he is able to abide by our rules without being a potential threat." Los Angeles Sparks star Cameron Brink also weighed in on the controversy surrounding Kanter, calling the debate over transgender athletes "non-issue" for the WNBA and suggesting the retired NBA center was "just trying to stay relevant." LA SPARKS STAR DIRECTS EXPLICIT RANT AT ENES KANTER FREEDOM OVER TRANS DEBATE: 'STUPID PIECE OF S---' Kanter fired back at Brink’s comments Thursday during an appearance on "Fox News @ Night." "You guys are the one that [have] been advocating about male[s] playing in your league or against your team. Well here I am, I have arrived and I have every right to play because I identify as a woman," he said, before then accusing Brink of taking a position he characterized as inconsistent with support for transgender athletes. "For you to come out and act like I shouldn't be playing, you are anti-trans and it is unacceptable." Kanter also responded to Megan Rapinoe. The two-time Women’s World Cup champion with the U.S. women’s national team had questioned his assertion that he was "just out there to protect women." "Well, oh my God, thank you so much because that’s what we were asking for. In fairness, you did warn us about men forcing their way into WNBA spaces, and lo and behold," Rapinoe said. ENES KANTER FREEDOM EJECTED FROM SKY-FEVER GAME AFTER VERBAL ALTERCATION WITH NATASHA CLOUD "I grew up playing soccer and you are one of those female athletes [who] advocated [for] males playing in women's sports, so here I am. I am offering you $5 million to any charity you want, if you beat me one-on-one in soccer." The confrontation with Cloud last Sunday unfolded shortly after she scored in the paint with less than two minutes remaining in the third quarter. The Fever called timeout and Cloud celebrated with teammate Aicha Coulibaly before turning and walking toward Freedom along the baseline. Cloud, who led the WNBA in assists in 2022, began shouting and pointing toward the 34-year-old Freedom as she approached him. Freedom then rose from his seat and stepped onto the court with his arms extended as security personnel and several Sky players moved between them. "It was pretty clear to us that his purpose of coming here was trying to be provocative and just see how much attention he could get and stir up and create," Alter told reporters. Kanter said he would be willing to speak directly with Cloud about the incident. "Of course I would sit down and talk to her," Kanter told "Fox News @ Night" host Trace Gallagher. articles.title: Lopetegui saca pecho con la segunda estrella: "Tenemos que estar muy orgullosos"
articles.standfirst: El ex seleccionador atiende a Radio MARCA para repasar el histórico Mundial de España, el regreso de Morata al fútbol español y la vuelta de Mourinho al Real Madrid
articles.summary: El ex seleccionador atiende a Radio MARCA para repasar el histórico Mundial de España, el regreso de Morata al fútbol español y la vuelta de Mourinho al Real Madrid, entre otras cosas
articles.body: Julen Lopetegui vive un momento especial. El técnico español acaba de completar con Qatar una etapa histórica, después de conseguir la clasificación para el Mundial, y ya tiene la mirada puesta en la próxima Copa del Golfo. En una entrevista en 'El Programa de Ortega', el ex seleccionador nacional ha repasado, además del éxito de la selección española, el regreso de Álvaro Morata y Mourinho a LaLiga. "Estamos muy contentos de nuestro periplo qatarí. Ha sido una experiencia profesional y personal muy bonita, muy intensa y muy interesante", explicó Lopetegui. Y añade: "Ahora hemos dejado atrás el Mundial, la clasificación histórica y lo conseguido y estamos centrados en la próxima Copa del Golfo". Lopetegui no escondió su satisfacción por el éxito de España en el Mundial. El técnico considera que la selección ha culminado un ciclo extraordinario y pone en valor la dificultad de encadenar grandes títulos. "Conseguir la segunda estrella creo que es algo maravilloso para todo el fútbol español y para una generación de futbolistas, para un cuerpo técnico que lo lleva haciendo maravillosamente bien", señaló. El entrenador destacó la continuidad del proyecto español y recordó los éxitos anteriores: "No solo en este Mundial, sino también en la Copa de Naciones, en la Eurocopa". Para Lopetegui, la conquista del Mundial supone "cerrar el círculo de tres competiciones consecutivas ganándolas". Y quiso poner el foco en la dificultad de la gesta: "Eso realmente es muy, muy difícil". "Conseguir ser una gran selección es muy difícil, pero conseguir ganar ya es realmente mucho más complejo", sentenció. El técnico quiso felicitar expresamente al seleccionador y a todo su equipo de trabajo: "A Luis, a todo su staff y a toda esta generación de futbolistas que nos ha hecho disfrutar una barbaridad". Lopetegui también valoró el regreso de José Mourinho al Real Madrid. El técnico español considera que el portugués cuenta con una ventaja importante: conoce perfectamente el club. "Es alguien que conoce perfectamente la casa. Él estuvo ya hace tiempo ahí", explicó. Además, Lopetegui considera que Mourinho regresa con más experiencia y madurez: "Vuelve con unos años más de experiencia, más maduro y conociendo la casa perfectamente. Creo que es una ventaja añadida que tienen tanto el Real Madrid como José". "Seguro que está más que capacitado para poder hacer un año bueno y bonito. Ojalá que así sea", añadió para concluir.

articles.title: España domina a Países Bajos y jugará la final del Mundial
articles.standfirst: El equipo nacional resistió una gran salida y un fuerte final de los anfitriones
articles.summary: El equipo nacional resistió una gran salida y un fuerte final de los anfitriones
articles.body: La selección española jugará la final del Campeonato del Mundo tras haber superado por 4-3 a Países Bajos, segundo equipo del ranking mundial, campeón olímpico y anfitrión de la competición. El equipo de Max Caldas consiguió superar con bien un fortísimo inicio local y un angustioso final, en el que los neerlandeses recortaron dos goles desde una ventaja española de 1-4. Será la primera final mundialista española desde 1998. En aquella final se cayó ante Países Bajos, que también eran locales, por 3-2. Esta vez se ha dado la vuelta al partido. El portero Luis Calzado fue el héroe de los primeros minutos del encuentro, salvando varias ocasiones locales en los primeros cinco minutos. Después, el equipo español fue sacudiéndose el dominio local. Las primeras ocasiones españolas llegaron al final del primer cuarto, pero al descanso se llegó con 1-0 local, obra de Jip Janssen. Pero partido cambió de signo en el segundo tiempo. 'Chefo' Basterra empató el encuentro con un sutil toque tras un saque de falta. Ya en el último cuarto Duco Telgenkamp recibió 10 minutos de exclusión por agresión y cuando los locales se estaban recomponiendo de nuevo Basterra, rematando en segundo palo una gran acción ofensiva de líneas muy amplias, puso el 1-2. Pepe Cunill puso el 1-3 de penalti córner y Basterra culminó su 'hat trick' a falta de 5:47. Pero los neerlandeses demostraron que son uno de los grandes equipos mundiales. Jip Janssen y Joep De Mol descontaron dos goles, el último a falta de 1:03, pero de nuevo Calzado y una gran gestión defensiva en el último minuto aseguraron el triunfo. La final se jugará a las 16:30 del domingo 30 entre España y el vencedor de la semifinal Alemania-Argentina.

articles.title: Lions may have found the perfect player to pair with Aidan Hutchinson
articles.summary: The Detroit Lions' hopes on this player may come true.
articles.body:
Ever since Aidan Hutchinson came on the scene with the Detroit Lions in 2022, he's been nothing but a blockbuster talent. Aside from the season where he was injured for most of the run, he's been steady with numbers and is considered one of the best defensive ends in the league.

Hutchinson, to date, has clocked 176 total tackles and 43 career sacks. But, the Lions have never really been serious about getting him a proper, long-term complement, until now.

During the NFL Draft this year, general manager Brad Holmes got serious about finding something to work with Hutchinson. He nabbed edge rusher Derrick Moore in the second round of the draft with the team's No. 44 selection.

Detroit Lions' Derrick Moore is already making an impression

Now, Moore is already impressing. Eric Woodyard of ESPN praises the pick in a feature discussing all of the NFL rookies and how they're performing .

"Although Moore missed a couple weeks of training camp with a minor groin strain, he has caused problems off the edge this preseason," he notes in the piece. "He logged a couple tackles with a sack and a forced fumble in his preseason debut against Washington."

Woodyard adds that "Moore is expected to contribute to Detroit's edge rusher rotation immediately opposite Aidan Hutchinson."

Yes, that is the expectation. But, what's nice is that what the Lions are seeing from Moore when he's healthy is proving that they did the right thing by picking him for their lineup. He could really be the Hutchinson complement for which they've been waiting.

articles.title: 2028 blue-chip LB Landon Miller locks in Oregon game day visit
articles.summary: Oregon has locked in a game day visit for blue-chip 2028 linebacker Landon Miller, bring the De La Salle defender to Eugene for a mid-October clash.
articles.body:
The Oregon Ducks are continuing to stack game day visits for the fall, and they are turning to a familiar high school program in California to get ahead in a key 2028 recruiting race.

Four-star linebacker Landon Miller is set to make a trip up to Eugene. Miller has lined up several visits for the fall, including a trip to Oregon on Oct. 10 when the Ducks host UCLA. Miller has also scheduled visits to California, USC and Notre Dame, and is working on visits to Michigan and Ohio State as well.

Oregon is an early contender for Miller after establishing a connection with the De La Salle tackler. He has already made multiple trips to visit the campus and is regularly in contact with Dan Lanning , defensive coordinator Chris Hampton and inside linebackers coach Brian Michalowski . The Ducks have done good work out of De La Salle High School in the past, and Matthew Johnson , a De La Salle alum, is in line for a big role on the Ducks' defense this season.

Miller is the No. 11 linebacker in the 2028 class, per Rivals. USC and Ohio State could be the biggest competition in the race for the Ducks. He finished his sophomore season with 38 tackles, two sacks and an interception, despite missing five games with an injury. Miller is quick and athletic, and could play multiple roles in Oregon's defense well.

Oregon is working hard to secure top talents from California early in the 2028 recruiting cycle. The Ducks have seen more talent stay home with USC, UCLA and California in recent years, but the Ducks are still recruiting well in the state. The Ducks are also in on four-star safety Ca'ron Williams , four-star quarterback Josiah Boyd , four-star safety Jordan Hicks , and several more.

There is plenty of time for these recruitments to play out, but the Ducks have made a point to establish contact earlier in the process. After locking down visits for important Big Ten matchups in Eugene, the Ducks should be able to send a statement to the California recruits, including Miller, especially against UCLA.

The Ducks have stacked visits for some of their big matchups, and UCLA is shaping up to be a big recruiting day. In addition to Miller, Oregon will also host several top 2028 recruits, including wideout Jayce Halasz , quarterback Tristin Gaines , edge rusher Kameron McGee , and many more.

articles.title: Kansas City Chiefs: Could Move on from 27-Year-Old CB
articles.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs cornerback Kristian Fulton had a rough first season with the team. He missed most of training camp while recovering from a knee cleanu...
articles.body:
The Kansas City Chiefs cornerback Kristian Fulton had a rough first season with the team. He missed most of training camp while recovering from a knee cleanup procedure and lost the starting job. The 27-year-old Fulton suffered an ankle injury in Week 2, causing him to miss Weeks 3-5 and be a healthy scratch in Weeks 6-9 and 13-14. He finished with 16 tackles and six pass deflections across eight games, two starts, and 208 defensive snaps.

With Mansoor Delane and Nohl Williams expected to be the team's top two cornerbacks and L'Jarius Sneed back in Kansas City, Kristian Fulton is currently slotted as a third-stringer, which is a lot of money to pay someone making $10 million.

The Kansas City Chiefs could move on from a 27-year-old CB

In an NFL.com article, Kevin Patra identified 22 players who could either be traded or released during roster cuts. For the Chiefs, he named Kristian Fulton , noting that Brett Veach would likely trade him for draft compensation rather than cut him outright. Patra also added that if a team needed cornerback help, it would inquire about Fulton, who was solid in his eight appearances last season.

"I don't think general manager Brett Veach will outright cut Fulton, who was solid in eight games last season, but if I was a team needing corner help, I'd inquire about a trade," Patra said.

Here's what a trading team would inherit contractually

Kristian Fulton enters the final year of his two-year, $20 million contract and is scheduled to earn a $9.75 million base salary, $5 million guaranteed, and $10 million in cash, while incurring a $13 million cap hit, per Over The Cap . A trading team would inherit the base salary and guaranteed money, but not the $250,000 workout bonus, essentially making it a one-year, $9.75 million deal with $5 million guaranteed.

articles.body:
The Chicago Cubs are set to begin a weekend series against the Cincinnati Reds on Friday afternoon.

Chicago's last game came Wednesday when the Cubs fell 2-0 to the Arizona Diamondbacks.

Ahead of Friday's game, which will feature Reds right-hander Rhett Lowder against Cubs righty David Peterson, manager Craig Counsell made a few changes to his lineup.

On Wednesday, Bregman started at first base and hit third in the lineup.

For Friday's series opener, he'll move back one spot and bat cleanup while also starting at third base. He'll hit behind Pete Crow-Armstrong, Seiya Suzuki and Michael Busch.

Via Underdog MLB: "Cubs 8/28 P. Crow-Armstrong CF S. Suzuki RF M. Busch 1B A. Bregman 3B I. Happ LF N. Hoerner SS P. Ramírez 2B M. Conforto DH C. Kelly C D. Peterson SP."

Chicago signed Bregman to a five-year, $175 million deal this past offseason after he spent one season with the Boston Red Sox . His 2026 campaign has featured some ups and downs.

He enters Friday batting .252 across 131 games and leads the majors with 599 plate appearances. He's recorded 75 runs, 131 hits, 19 home runs and 69 RBIs while slugging .412 with a .755 OPS.

While Bregman has still put together a solid season, his hitting numbers have declined across the board, with some sitting at career lows.

Chicago is 76-58 overall and sits firmly in second place in the NL Central, trailing the Milwaukee Brewers by 7.0 games after cutting the deficit to nearly three games just a week ago.

Nonetheless, the Cubs hold a two-game lead over the Philadelphia Phillies for the top Wild Card spot. That position could prove important because the higher seed hosts all three games of the best-of-three Wild Card Series.

articles.title: Columbus Crew part ways with midfielder Daniel Gazdag
articles.summary: The Columbus Crew are buying out Daniel Gazdag's contract as the midfielder reportedly heads to New England.
articles.body:
Daniel Gazdag's tenure with the Crew is over.

The Dispatch has confirmed a report by the Athletic that Gazdag's contract, which runs through 2027, is being bought out by the Crew to make him a free agent. The Athletic report says Gazdag , 30, is finalizing a deal to join the New England Revolution.

New England plays the Crew on Aug. 30 at ScottsMiracle-Gro Field, and it's unknown whether Gazdag will be available for the Revolution.

The Dispatch has also confirmed a separate report by The Athletic saying the Crew are in advanced talks to sign Uruguayan attacking midfielder Santi Rodriguez from Botafago of Brazil's Serie A. Rodriguez would fill the designated player spot opened by Gazdag's departure.

Gazdag's tenure with the Crew was largely underwhelming after he was acquired for $4 million in a cash-for-player trade April 9, 2025 with the Philadelphia Union. The Hungarian midfielder left Philadelphia as the Union's franchise leader in goals (59) while also leading the club in all-time winning goals (14).

Prior to his exit, Gazdag filled one of the Crew's three designated player spots along with recently acquired forward Brais Mendez and forward Wessam Abou Ali , who's out for the season after surgery to repair an ACL tear.

articles.title: Raiders Get Tom Brady’s No-Nonsense Prep Tip Revealed by Kirk Cousins
articles.summary: Kirk Cousins is poised to be the starting quarterback for the Las Vegas Raiders in 2026. The veteran joined the franchise after he was released by the Atlant...
articles.body:
Kirk Cousins is poised to be the starting quarterback for the Las Vegas Raiders in 2026. The veteran joined the franchise after he was released by the Atlanta Falcons in the off-season.

Despite the Raiders having drafted No. 1 overall Fernando Mendoza in the 2026 NFL Draft, Cousins is slated to take the starting job, though no official announcement has been made. He recently talked about what one former legendary quarterback told the team.

Kirk Cousins reveals Tom Brady's message about Raiders' preparation

During a recent press conference , Cousins talked about the team's preseason preparation approach. He revealed that legendary NFL quarterback and Raiders minority owner Tom Brady shared a message with the team regarding their preseason preparations. The New England Patriots legend said that every team does preseason, and that it is the minimal thing to do.

Cousins said, "It's been a productive training camp and a productive preseason. But as Tom Brady said when he spoke to us, one of many good things he told us, everybody has training camp, and everybody has preseason games. To think that you're somehow getting ahead of everyone else just because you went out to practice is a mistake. There is no edge there, because everybody else is doing that too."

The Raiders are doing their best to prepare for the 2026 season and are looking to move on from a poor 2025 season. One of the key decisions the franchise has taken is to make Cousins the starter instead of Mendoza. The decision is to let Mendoza learn from the veteran, and prepare him for the future, which earlier won the approval of former NFL star Jason Kelce .

Brady had previously emphasized that players must work hard on his Instagram Story. He said , "Preseason… Regular season… I never wanted to be taken off the field. Practice makes perfect… Too many people looking for easy ways out these days. When you're a football player, and it's football season, your job is to play football."

Cousins had also talked about how one call from Brady changed his life.

Kirk Cousins reveals Tom Brady convinced him to join Raiders

In an appearance on "Good Morning Football", Cousins revealed that Brady convinced him to join the Raiders through a FaceTime call. He said , "You know me, I'm going to do my homework before I sign somewhere. So, I had a lot of conversations with people here and there with the Raiders' organization."

He added, "One of those conversations was with Tom. I texted him and asked him to call me when he could. He actually FaceTimed me. I was at youth baseball practice. So, I stepped away and just FaceTimed with Tom for a little bit, just to get on the same page and the vision for the organization and kind of what he saw ahead and if I would be a good fit for it or not."

The quarterback dubbed that exchange a life-giving call and shared that it eventually inspired him to join the Raiders.

Cousins continued, "I got off the call, and I called my wife and I said, 'That was a really life-giving call with Tom.' He gets it. He's been where I've been, and then some. I think he understands what it needs to look like and what it will look like. I really felt a shot in the arm after talking with him and I felt that was a big nudge for me to come to Vegas."

Kirk Cousins will now prepare for the next season, with much expectations on him.

articles.body:
Vanderbilt announced Aug. 28 that it has extended its radio partnership with Cromwell Media , which has broadcast various Commodores sporting events for the last six years.

As part of the multiyear extension there will be weekly programming and 102.5 FM will continue as the main flagship station for Vanderbilt football , men's basketball and baseball games. Also, 94.9 FM will broadcast all Vanderbilt women's basketball games and will air broadcasts when conflicts occur with the Nashville Predators schedule.

"We're incredibly proud to continue our partnership with Cromwell Media and provide Commodore fans across Middle Tennessee with a home for Vanderbilt Athletics," said Sean Ferretti, general manager of Vanderbilt Sports Properties, in a school release. "Vanderbilt has a rich tradition on the airwaves in Music City, and we're excited to build on that legacy alongside a tremendous partner in Cromwell Media. With 102.5 The Game and 94.9 The Fan, Commodore fans will continue to have outstanding access to the teams they love throughout the region."

The Commodore Hour radio show will air at 6 p.m. on Monday, beginning Aug. 31.

articles.title: The 3 Vikings Draft Picks with an Iffy Status Going into the NFL’s Cut Weekend
articles.summary: Soon enough, the Minnesota Vikings will need to go from 91 players to 53 players. Shuffling some guys over to […]
articles.body:
Soon enough, the Minnesota Vikings will need to go from 91 players to 53 players. Shuffling some guys over to the 16-player practice squad is going to help alleviate the pain, but there's only so much that spot can help.

Most of the Vikings draft picks are going to get onto the final roster that gets announced on Sunday, August 30th. In fact, several are moving into prominent roles, with LB Jake Golday and FB Max Bredeson standing out as having particularly promising offseasons. So, too, do defensive linemen Caleb Banks and Domonique Orange appear ready for Week 1 work . Are some of the Vikings draft picks in danger of missing the roster altogether?

3 Vikings Draft Picks with an Iffy Roster Status

3rd-Round OT Caleb Tiernan is not going to be cut. He's being included, though, due to an injury that's being described as a week-to-week issue by Kevin O'Connell .

Is the towering tackle going to be available for that Week 1 game? That's the goal. If there's uncertainty, then maybe he gets shuffled off the 53-man roster into the infirmary. Doing so clears a roster slot on a short-term basis. The benefit from a roster construction perspective is that Tiernan could be kept within the team's orbit without demanding a roster spot in the initial weeks of the 2026 season.

Not a locked-in reality, just something that's possible. Health is the only thing that's going to be an issue for Tiernan getting included among those official 53 guys.

Demond Claiborne is in the running for being the fastest player on the roster. At the very least, he's the fastest running back. He may not get kept around, though.

Both of Aaron Jones and Jordan Mason are better and higher on the depth chart. What about returning runner Zavier Scott ? He's a versatile talent who boasts good size, soft hands, and past experience in this offense. If he's the RB3, then Claiborne is in a tricky position since there's no guarantee that an RB4 sticks around.

Demond Claiborne is likely to make the final roster. What's been concerning, though, is some ball security issues alongside some inefficient work in the preseason games. He's said to be a work in progress in the passing game. Trying to slide him down to the practice squad means seeing him at a high risk of getting poached.

Note that Minnesota traded up into the 6th to pick Demond Claiborne.

The rough-and-tough offensive lineman is a long shot to get onto the final roster.

Chosen in the 7th Round, Gavin Gerhardt was always facing an uphill battle. Neither C1 Blake Brandel nor C2 Michael Jurgens are so formidable so as to be insurmountable. The issue, though, is that Gerhardt doesn't appear ready to help early within his career.

Look for him to marinate on the practice squad as a rookie before then pushing for more in 2027 and beyond. In time, Gerhardt's job will be to function as iOL depth on the active roster.

Manchester City and Crystal Palace have confirmed their starting lineups ahead of tonight's match at Selhurst Park. Enzo Maresca's side will be aiming to continue building momentum after their late 2-1 win over Bournemouth last weekend. The team spirit that City showed to score two late goals was fantastic and could carry them a long way this season. Orazio Accomando has now reported that it is Crystal Palace who have swooped in for Solet. They are ready to offer a fee worth €25 million to sign the defender.

Besides, Crystal Palace could soon need a defensive addition and Solet could be a clever addition indeed and he would come at an affordable fee.

articles.title: Scottie Scheffler’s advice for amateur golfers to become more consistent when chipping and pitching
articles.summary: Scottie Scheffler is one of the very best in the game around the greens, if not the best. Scheffler has won 21 times on the PGA Tour since February 2022, inc...
articles.body:
Scottie Scheffler is one of the very best in the game around the greens, if not the best.

Scheffler has won 21 times on the PGA Tour since February 2022, including four major championships.

One of the main reasons for his success is his exceptional short game.

Scottie Scheffler has mastered every single short game shot around the greens so that when on the rare occasion he is not striking the ball well, he can still score and keep himself in tournaments.

The key to the 30-year-old world number one's stunning short game is a simple motion, one that he has honed throughout the years to near perfection.

Now you can learn from how the best player in the world goes about chipping and pitching the ball.

Scottie Scheffler's advice for amateurs to become more consistent when chipping

When writing an instructional column for Golf Digest, the 30-year-old explained how the key to better chipping is ensuring that the hands are not active throughout the shot.

" Getting better around the greens means improving your average result, " Scheffler began.

" To get more consistent, rethink how you use your hands on these shots. For example, to hit a stock bunker shot, I'll set up with the ball forward in my stance and my hands slightly behind it so the shaft is leaning away from the target.

" Then I'll make a centered turn back and through with a lot less wrist hinge and release than a lot of players use. You don't need to use your hands all that much to hit a good shot.

" The only time my hands are more active is if I want more spin. I'll use them to speed up the clubhead's release. "

The same is true for pitching, says Scheffler

The same principle for chipping applies to pitching.

" For a pitch shot, the same holds true, " the world number one said.

" My hands aren't all that involved. I like to hit this "hook spinner", because it makes the ball land and roll out under control.

" To execute it, set up with the face square and feel like you're returning the shaft to the same position it was at address as you strike the ball.

" The idea is that you're not pulling the handle and using hand action to get the club back to the ball. Keep turning your chest and rotating the club, and you'll skid the clubhead along the ground and pick the ball clean.

" If you're taking big divots when you hit pitch shots, you're probably using your hands too much. "

articles.title: F1 Today | Ferrari told to prioritize Hamilton, Kelly Piquet shares emotional message
articles.summary: From Ferrari once again being urged to support Lewis Hamilton over Charles Leclerc to Kelly Piquet's emotional message on social media, GPblog recaps the bes...
articles.body:
From Ferrari once again being urged to support Lewis Hamilton over Charles Leclerc to Kelly Piquet 's emotional message on social media, GPblog recaps the best news of the day from the world of Formula 1 .

Ferrari told to back Hamilton over Leclerc to have an 'impact on title battle'

After Hamilton's angry team radio messages at the Dutch Grand Prix, where he asked his team to tell Leclerc to let him past while running an alternative strategy, Rob Smedley argued that the Scuderia needs to back the British driver if it wants to have a real impact on this year's title battle.

He said on the High Performance Racing Podcast: "As hard as that is for Charles and the team that sits on that side of the garage with Charles and all the rest of it, they all work for Ferrari."

Smedley continued: "Lewis has had the better run and done the better job. And I think if they're going to steal points from Mercedes, they're going to do that as a team.

"They haven't got the best car consistently, but they have on occasions got the best car, and they're going to make it count then, and they're going to make sure that Lewis wins. On all the other occasions, they're just going to make sure that they maximize Lewis' points.

"This is just about doing what is the sensible thing for the team and trying to maximize Ferrari's position in the world championship," he concluded.

Hamilton is currently tied on points with his former teammate, George Russell, in the drivers' standings, 59 points behind Kimi Antonelli.

Piquet shares a moving message about daughter Penelope and receives support from Verstappen

On social media, the partner of Max Verstappen , Kelly Piquet, shared an emotional message dedicated to her first daughter, Penelope.

She did not go into specifics about what happened over the last month since Penelope's birthday, but wrote extensively about the lessons motherhood has taught her.

Piquet also addresses her daughter directly. "My P, I will always listen to you, stand up for you, protect your gentleness, and remind you that your feelings matter. I hope your seventh year brings you the peace, freedom, and carefree joy that every little girl deserves."

articles.title: Orioles could make bold Craig Albernaz decision for one reason
articles.summary: The Orioles could go one-and-done with Albernaz in one scenario.
articles.body:
The Baltimore Orioles are having a very disappointing season compared to expectations. Coming into the year, this was supposed to be a return to the playoffs.

Instead, the Orioles have squandered a good chance in a wide-open AL and sit at 65-69 on the season with the likelihood of making the postseason slim. It's been a rough first season for Craig Albernaz as manager, and things could get worse from here.

Karl Rasmussen of Sports Illustrated believes the Orioles could decide to move on from Albernaz as manager after just one season if one thing happens: Baltimore struggles down the home stretch of the regular season.

Orioles could fire Craig Albernaz if home stretch goes poorly

"Albernaz was only just hired by the Orioles last offseason, but the team's struggles could spell an early end to his tenure," Rasmussen writes. "... It wouldn't be a surprise if Albernaz got a second season at the helm, but if Baltimore struggles down the stretch, the 43-year-old could wind up as being a one-and-done."

The Orioles are on the outside looking in for the MLB postseason, but in a weak American League, they're just 3.0 games out.

It would not be a total surprise if they got hot to end the season and wound up making the postseason, taking the third and final Wild Card spot.

Being the third Wild Card team in the AL would be a good thing, as that team will most likely face the winner of the AL West, a division whose leader is at .500 on August 28.

Making the postseason is within the realm of possibility for the Orioles and Albernaz. But there's also a scenario in which the Orioles struggle in September and fall well out of the postseason hunt.

That, combined with the overall disappointment of this iteration of the Orioles, which might be coming to an end after the trade of Adley Rutschman, could lead to Albernaz getting fired after just one season.

The Orioles can't fully start another rebuild; it would be way too depressing. So, the Orioles might decide to give it one more chance in 2027 with Albernaz and this version of the Orioles.

But if things go south and end the regular season for the Orioles, then Albernaz could wind up being relieved of his duties following the 2026 season in a brutal one-and-done stint as manager for the first time in his career.

articles.title: Freshman CB showcasing elite traits with Washington football
articles.summary: Washington Huskies secondary coach John Richardson has been pleased with what he's seen from freshman CB Rahsjon Duncan.
articles.body:
One of Washington's top-ranked signees in the 2026 class, four-star cornerback Rahsjon Duncan, wasn't able to enroll with the Huskies until June and is getting himself acclimated to the college level ahead of his freshman season on Montlake.

After arriving as the No. 57 overall prospect and No. 6 cornerback in the nation, according to Rivals, Duncan has certainly looked the part during fall camp, even though he hasn't had much production to show for it on the stat sheet.

In what appears to be a room rich with young talent, including Duncan's classmates Jeron Jones and Elijah Durr, secondary coach John Richardson has been very pleased with the progress of the product of McClymonds High School in Oakland, California.

"Rahsjon is, first of all, a phenomenal athlete and very physical," Richardson said on Friday. "So for him, it's just getting acclimated since he got here in June, getting his body going and stuff like that, just to the college regimen. But athletically, man, he's doing great things, but just trying to get him focused and disciplined on those types of things. But it's nothing different than Dylan (Robinson) first coming in."

"The only difference is Dylan is like 6-foot-3, 6-foot-4; he's weighing 210 pounds, something crazy. So, it's just different body types, but Duncan is the same type of athlete, just athletic, and we'll get him going too."

When asked about Duncan's lateral speed, Richardson had more praise for the freshman, who could carve out a role for himself with the Huskies this fall.

"He's built very well, he can go out there and run track, and he's probably a 10.4- 10.5 (100-meter dash) kid on the track. Typically, some guys are just straight ahead, but he can definitely move laterally, and he can change direction and pick up speed fast. So for him, he's built well; he comes from a great program in McClymonds, where (UW alum) Marcus Peters is from, who's the head coach there as well. I'm pretty sure he's feeling the pressure from his old coach about how you need to play out here. So, I've been mainly just teaching him and growing him, and then he'll get acclimated and get going, too."

articles.title: Carl Sandburg College breaks ground on new athletic hub
articles.summary: Carl Sandburg College has broken ground on the Charger Center, a massive new athletic and community complex in Galesburg.
articles.body:
Carl Sandburg College marked a major milestone in its athletic facilities expansion with a groundbreaking ceremony for the Charger Center on Aug. 27.

The event celebrated the start of construction on the planned facility, according to a community announcement. Initial work on the project began earlier this month on the Galesburg campus.

The Charger Center is planned as a 70,204-square-foot athletic and conference complex that will become the new home for Sandburg's athletic programs while also supporting academic activities and community events.

College officials expect the facility to open in late 2027.

New athletic and community space planned

The Charger Center was designed by Legat Architects and will be built in the southeast portion of campus adjacent to Building G.

Its front entrance will face across Tom L. Wilson Blvd. toward the rest of the campus. Turf playing fields for baseball, softball and soccer are planned on the south side of the building.

Facilities include gyms, training areas and esports

Plans for the Charger Center include two wood-floor gymnasiums that can host athletic competitions and large events, as well as a third gymnasium with multi-purpose flooring.

Additional features will include fitness and training areas, a golf simulator room, an esports arena, multi-purpose spaces and indoor turf areas supporting several athletic programs.

Photos shared by the college after the ceremony showed participants gathering on the construction site as work moves forward on a project intended to expand athletic, academic and community-use opportunities on campus, according to the announcement.

articles.title: Former Florida center Micah Handlogten commits to SEC rival Ole Miss
articles.summary: Former Florida center Micah Handlogten has committed to Ole Miss as he seeks a fifth season of college eligibility.
articles.body:
Former Florida center Micah Handlogten has found a new home, although his return to college basketball still depends on receiving another year of eligibility.

Handlogten has committed to Ole Miss, according to multiple reports, giving the 7-foot-1-inch big man a chance to remain in the SEC after spending the past three seasons with the Gators. He entered the transfer portal in April following Florida's 2025-26 season.

One question surrounding Handlogten's eligibility is whether he signed an Exhibit 10 contract with the Utah Jazz. There are conflicting reports on whether Handlogten actually put pen to paper, which could hurt his case for a return to the college ranks.

Before coming to Florida, Handlogten spent his freshman year at Marshall, where he averaged 7.6 points, 9.8 rebounds and 2.3 blocks per game and was named the Sun Belt Freshman of the Year.

He played in all three seasons he was with the Florida Gators , but a gruesome broken leg suffered in the 2024 SEC Tournament championship game kept him out for most of the following 2024-25 season. He gave up his redshirt to return in February and help Florida's frontcourt while Alex Condon dealt with an injury.

Handlogten appeared in 34 games for Florida last season, averaging 4.1 points, 5.9 rebounds and 0.9 blocks in 14.8 minutes per game. He spent most of the season backing up Rueben Chinyelu but remained an important piece of Todd Golden's frontcourt rotation. He finished his Florida career with 83 appearances and 34 starts over three seasons.

Ole Miss landed Handlogten over NC State and Southern California . If his eligibility bid is successful, Handlogten won't have to wait long to see his former team. Ole Miss is scheduled to visit Florida in late February, setting up a potential return to the O'Connell Center for a player who helped the Gators capture the 2025 national championship.

articles.title: Former elite safety commit could visit Florida State this weekend
articles.summary: Four-star safety Mekhi Williams was committed to FSU before flipping to Wisconsin. However, he could be in Tallahassee this weekend.
articles.body:
2027 four-star safety Mekhi Williams was a longtime commit for Florida State . However, he decided to flip his pledge to the Wisconsin Badgers early this summer. That hasn't stopped the communication between him and the Seminoles.

"Well, as of right now, my recruitment's shut down, but I'm still gonna keep them right now inside the loop because they're still a big part — they were a big part for me and my recruitment and everything. I just don't want to close that door or break anything," Williams said in June .

That was after the 6-foot-2.5, 160-pounder attended a camp in Tallahassee. He also mentioned then that a possible visit during the season could happen. According to Zach Blostein of 247Sports , that might take place this weekend when FSU plays the New Mexico State Aggies.

A source told 247Sports on Friday morning that there is a 50-50 chance that Top247 Wisconsin safety commit Mekhi Williams, a former Florida State commit, makes it to Saturday's game. If he makes it in, it'll mark the first time he has visited FSU since flipping from the Seminoles over the summer.

Williams has stated that he's completely locked in with Wisconsin. That may be the case, but the more Florida State stays in the picture, the stronger the possibility is for a possible flip back, especially if they have a successful season.

FSU has four-star Ta'Shawn Poole and three-star ball hawk Jemari Foreman at the safety spot committed in the 2027 cycle. That's an excellent haul in itself at the position, but if they could get Williams back, that would significantly boost what they're bringing in next year.

Williams is the No. 219 prospect nationally and the No. 18 safety. He's also the No. 25 recruit in the state of Florida.

articles.title: Presidents Cup teams to make overlapping Medinah scouting trips in September
articles.summary: Both U.S. and International Presidents Cup teams are visiting Medinah No. 3 to scout the course and build team unity ahead of next month's competition.
articles.body:
ATLANTA – Medinah No. 3 should be selling tickets to watch the golfers playing the course, Sept. 9-11.

Golfweek has learned that both the U.S. and International Teams for the 2026 Presidents Cup will be making two-day scouting trips to the host venue in Chicago.

The International Team is expected to show up first (Sept. 9-10), followed by the U.S. team (Sept. 10-11), with both sharing the property for one day.

"The team felt it would be beneficial to experience Medinah's updated layout firsthand," said U.S. Presidents Cup captain Brandt Snedeker. "Any opportunity to gain familiarity with the course and better understand how it may play in a team competition setting is valuable as we continue preparing for Presidents Cup week."

The final rosters will not be solidified until Snedeker and Geoff Ogilvy, the International Team captain, both make their captain's picks on Tuesday. Adam Scott, who is expected to be on the International Team for a record 12 th time, said that in the past a team trip beforehand had been optional but that this one is mandatory. A source close to the International Team confirmed that players have given assurances they will attend. Min Woo Lee mentioned on Thursday in his post-round press conference that he planned to attend.

Ogilvy, who played in three Presidents Cups and was a vice captain in the past, said that one of the challenges in the past was unifying a team made up of players from various countries and who spoke different languages in such a short window of time once they gathered the week of the Presidents Cup. "We always felt like we became a team by Saturday," he once said.

The scouting trips are as much about team bonding and camaraderie as figuring out if certain pairings might work.

"The golf isn't what's important, honestly," Scott said. "The investment is in the guys getting together and feeling comfortable and taking away any trepidation of playing with a partner and not feeling comfortable saying something. It's a chance to set some barriers and lay down the ground rules for everyone."

Until the U.S. side officially is selected, a source familiar with the U.S. plans said it is premature to say that the entire team will participate in its reconnaissance mission but the U.S. side is hopeful that will be the case.

An advanced practice session to learn the layout, test potential team pairings and team building has started to become standard operating procedure for the teams competing in international competition. Two-time winning European Ryder Cup captain Luke Donald called a similar trip ahead of the Ryder Cup a pivotal part of the Euros meshing as a team.

After finishing up the BMW PGA Championship in England last year, 11 members of the European Ryder Cup, caddies and captain Luke Donald boarded a flight for New York, where they met up with teammate Sepp Straka for a two-day reconnaissance trip to Bethpage Black ahead of the 45 th Ryder Cup. The U.S. side was criticized in defeat of not showing up to play Bethpage until the week of the biennial competition.

Two years ago, Jim Furyk, the U.S. Presidents Cup captain at the time, brought 11 members of the team to the Tour's now-defunct Napa, California, FedEx Cup Fall event for a bonding trip. As U.S. Ryder Cup captain, Keegan Bradley repeated the Napa trip.

The International side also has taken trips to Quail Hollow in 2022 and Royal Montreal in 2024 in recent years ahead of the Presidents Cup.

Medinah No. 3 underwent a dramatic renovation since the last time the PGA Tour has held an event there. Justin Thomas torched the course to a tune of a 72-hole total of 25 under at the 2019 BMW Championship. The reimagining of Medinah was orchestrated by Ogilvy and his design team at OCM and opened in late 2024. Could that provide an edge to the International Team, which has never won the Presidents Cup in the U.S. and last won the biennial competition in 1998?

Time will tell but suffice it to say, Ogilvy will be doling out plenty of local knowledge to his 12-man team on how he envisions the course he co-designed should be played.

articles.title: David Jablonski: Ohio State football: Lakota East grad moves from tackle to guard
articles.summary: Austin Siereveld doesn’t care where he plays on the Ohio State Buckeyes offensive line. “Wherever they want me,” he told reporters on Wednesday, Aug. 26, at...
articles.body:
Austin Siereveld doesn't care where he plays on the Ohio State Buckeyes offensive line.

"Wherever they want me," he told reporters on Wednesday, Aug. 26, at the Woody Hayes Athletic Center in Columbus.

Coach Ryan Day expects Siereveld, a 2023 Lakota East High School graduate, to start at right guard after playing left tackle last season. In a press conference Monday, Day said that was the current plan. It wouldn't be finalized until later in the week.

"He obviously spent a lot of time at tackle last year," Day said.

Now the 6-foot-5, 327-pound Siereveld is working on the interior of the line, Day said, and "getting more and more comfortable" as the Sept. 5 opener against Ball State approaches.

The other expected starters on the line are left guard Luke Montgomery, center Carson Hinzman, left tackle Ian Moore and right tackle Phillip Daniels. Everyone but Moore, who made one start in 2025, started most of last season.

One of the backups at guard is Wayne grad Joshua Padilla, who appeared in 13 games last season and started against Miami in the College Football Playoff.

Siereveld has built chemistry with the other linemen. He has a natural connection with Daniels, a Princeton High School graduate, because Siereveld grew up not far away in Liberty Township. Siereveld played next to Hinzman when Siereveld played guard two years ago.

"Now we can look at each other," Siereveld said of his fellow linemen, "and we already know what's going to happen."

This will be the third straight year Siereveld, Daniels and Hinzman have started together.

"It's very uncommon to have your three interior guys play for three years together," Siereveld said, "and we've got to take advantage of that. The connections we have are unreal. We vibe. We click."

Siereveld has played all over the line in his Ohio State career. After redshirting as a freshman in 2023, he played left and right guard in 2024, appearing in 16 games and making seven starts.

Last season, Siereveld was expected to play guard but was moved to left tackle. He made the All-Big Ten second team.

I thought I'd always be at guard," Siereveld said before the 2025 season, "but I'm just working on my craft every day. The coaches are helping me out when I ask questions. I'm just working every single day to try to be the best player I can be.

Siereveld started all 14 games for a team that finished 12-0 in the regular season before losing to Indiana in the Big Ten championship game and to Miami in the playoff quarterfinals. He totaled 810 snaps after playing 577 snaps in 2024.

"Last year was the first year I played one position all year," Siereveld said, "and I was just so comfortable."

"I was so used to guard in my first two years," Siereveld said. "Stepping out there was a challenge at first. Getting as many reps as possible, each week I was getting better and better."

The decision to move Siereveld back to guard was made so Ohio State could start junior Moore at left tackle.

Siereveld told offensive line coach Tyler Bowen he hated right guard because he was so used to left tackle, but his feeling soon changed.

"As you get more and more reps, you get more used to it," he said, "and I got comfortable with it."

For the second straight year, Siereveld will serve as a captain. Day announced seven captains for the 2026 season on Aug. 22. The others are wide receiver Brandon Inniss, defensive end Kenyatta Jackson Jr., safety Jaylen McClain, linebacker Payton Pierce, quarterback Julian Sayin and wide receiver Jeremiah Smith.

"This is a significant day for our program," Day said in a press release. "We have seven captains this year, the seventh time in Ohio State football history that we have had that many or more. Being voted a captain is one of the greatest honors in this program because it comes directly from your teammates. This group represents our team well, with leaders from different position groups, backgrounds, and experiences. All seven are returning players, including two captains from last year, and they understand our standard and what it means to carry our culture forward."

Only Siereveld and Inniss are returning captains. Players vote for captains and can choose from juniors, seniors or fifth-year players.

"It means a lot," Siereveld said. "Especially being from Ohio, it means even more. Shoutout to all the guys out there for trusting me and voting for me."

Liverpool have a chance to hijack a Chelsea deal but they're running out of time. It's something they simply have to do.

Liverpool need a midfielder. That should have been pretty clear to most already but Sunday's draw at Newcastle United hammered the point home in spectacular fashion.

The Reds were porous in the middle of the pitch, unable to stop counter-attacks and Newcastle consistently got chances to run directly at the back line. Having someone to stand in the middle would make a gigantic improvement to Liverpool's team as none of their current midfielders naturally do that.

But it's not easy to find a midfielder this late in a transfer window. Clubs don't like to sell when there's not really any chance of finding a suitable replacement - even if the offer is a good one.

It's why we can't fathom why Liverpool would pass up the chance to sign Lamine Camara. We're massive fans of the player - he's about as solid as it gets, with proven quality over multiple seasons, is still only 22...

There are very few midfielders in Europe who can simultaneously take on a large portion of the defensive workload and create chances for his team. Camara is arguably the best at it.

In fact, he's the only midfielder in the top five leagues who's in the top 10 per cent for share of the defensive workload and top 10 per cent for creating big chances for 25/26. And again, he's 22.

The other way of putting that is this: Camara is about as sure-fire a success as you can get with a transfer. He does everything to an above-average level for a top-five-league midfielder and is truly elite at the exact things Liverpool are after.

And here's the mad thing: he's available! Foot Mercato is one of several outlets reporting that Chelsea are pushing forward on a deal for Camara and that Liverpool have been offered a deal .

The Reds appear set to ignore this one, though, and move onto other targets. Camara, who would be perfect, looks set to join Chelsea as Liverpool sign an alternative - despite the fact any alternative would be more difficult to sign and almost certainly a worse fit.

articles.title: Juventus adds a wonderkid to their squad this summer
articles.summary: Juventus have signed Genk wonderkid Ali Camara, and he will start his career at the club with the youth teams this season while working his way towards the s...
articles.body:
Juventus have signed Genk wonderkid Ali Camara, and he will start his career at the club with the youth teams this season while working his way towards the senior side.

Camara has been one of the top teenagers in European football and has done well in Genk's youth system so far, which has led several clubs to follow his progress. The winger is just 18 and has been performing well in Belgium, where Juve have scouted him for a long time.

The Old Lady have now secured an agreement to add him to their squad. La Gazzetta dello Sport reports that they have agreed to pay between 1.5 and 2m euros for his signature, and he travelled to Turin yesterday to undergo his medical and complete the move.

The attacker is delighted to have moved to Juve, as he believes impressing with their Next Gen team will give him a chance to play for the senior side. That would provide him with an opportunity to represent one of the top clubs in the world.

Camara will initially focus on adapting to his new surroundings and continuing his development. Juventus believe he has the potential to progress through their system, which makes his arrival an investment in the future.

The Bianconeri also see investing in his signature as one of the best things they have done this summer. They will hope all goes well with his medical and that he completes the move without any issues.

Luciano Spalletti has a good first team squad, but the manager would love to hand debuts to some of the top players in the club's youth system. The more talented players Juventus can develop there, the greater the chance of promoting some of them to the first team.

Camara now has the opportunity to establish himself within the Next Gen team before attempting to make the step up to senior football. His performances will determine how quickly he can progress, but Juventus have already shown their belief in his potential by securing his signature.

For now, the 18-year-old will concentrate on developing with the youth setup and proving that he can eventually make the transition to the senior squad. Juventus will hope their latest investment can become another successful pathway from their youth system to the first team.
